verses.textEnNasb: In view of this I also do my best to maintain a blameless conscience both before God and before other people, always.
verses.textEn: So I strive always to keep my conscience clear before God and man.

verses.textZh: 过了几年我带着捐款回来赒济本国，同时也带了祭物，
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了几年我带着捐款回来赒济本国，同时也带了祭物，
verses.textZhCuv: 过了几年，我带着周济本国的捐项和供献的物上去。
verses.textEnNiv: "After an absence of several years, I came to Jerusalem to bring my people gifts for the poor and to present offerings.
verses.textEnEsv: Now after several years I came to bring alms to my nation and to present offerings.
verses.textEnNkjv: This being so, I myself always strive to have a conscience without offense toward God and men.
verses.textEnNlt: "After several years away, I returned to Jerusalem with money to aid my people and to offer sacrifices to God.
verses.textEnNasb: Now after several years I came to bring charitable gifts to my nation and to present offerings,
verses.textEn: "After an absence of several years, I came to Jerusalem to bring my people gifts for the poor and to present offerings.

verses.textZh: 他们看见我在殿里的时候，我已经行完了洁净礼，并没有和一大群人在一起，也没有生乱，
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们看见我在殿里的时候，我已经行完了洁净礼，并没有和一大群人在一起，也没有生乱，
verses.textZhCuv: 正献的时候，他们看见我在殿里已经洁净了，并没有聚众，也没有吵嚷，惟有几个从亚细亚来的犹太人。
verses.textEnNiv: I was ceremonially clean when they found me in the temple courts doing this. There was no crowd with me, nor was I involved in any disturbance.
verses.textEnEsv: While I was doing this, they found me purified in the temple, without any crowd or tumult. But some Jews from Asia—
verses.textEnNkjv: "Now after many years I came to bring alms and offerings to my nation,
verses.textEnNlt: My accusers saw me in the Temple as I was completing a purification ceremony. There was no crowd around me and no rioting.
verses.textEnNasb: in which they found me occupied in the temple, having been purified, without any crowd or uproar. But there were some Jews from Asia—
verses.textEn: I was ceremonially clean when they found me in the temple courts doing this. There was no crowd with me, nor was I involved in any disturbance.

verses.textZh: 只有几个从亚西亚来的犹太人而已。他们若有事要控告我，就应该到你面前来控告。
verses.textZhCnvs: 只有几个从亚西亚来的犹太人而已。他们若有事要控告我，就应该到你面前来控告。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们若有告我的事，就应当到你面前来告我。
verses.textEnNiv: But there are some Jews from the province of Asia, who ought to be here before you and bring charges if they have anything against me.
verses.textEnEsv: they ought to be here before you and to make an accusation, should they have anything against me.
verses.textEnNkjv: in the midst of which some Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with a mob nor with tumult.
verses.textEnNlt: But some Jews from the province of Asia were there—and they ought to be here to bring charges if they have anything against me!
verses.textEnNasb: who ought to have been present before you and to have been bringing charges, if they should have anything against me.
verses.textEn: But there are some Jews from the province of Asia, who ought to be here before you and bring charges if they have anything against me.

verses.textZh: 要不然，当我站在公议会中受审的时候，这些人若发现我有甚么罪行，早就亲自说出来了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 要不然，当我站在公议会中受审的时候，这些人若发现我有甚么罪行，早就亲自说出来了。
verses.textZhCuv: 即或不然，这些人若看出我站在公会前，有妄为的地方，他们自己也可以说明。
verses.textEnNiv: Or these who are here should state what crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin—
verses.textEnEsv: Or else let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council,
verses.textEnNkjv: They ought to have been here before you to object if they had anything against me.
verses.textEnNlt: Ask these men here what crime the Jewish high council found me guilty of,
verses.textEnNasb: Or else have these men themselves declare what violation they discovered when I stood before the Council,
verses.textEn: Or these who are here should state what crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin—

verses.textZh: 如果有的话，就是我站在他们中间所喊的：‘我今天在你们面前受审，是为了死人复活的事’那一句话。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 如果有的话，就是我站在他们中间所喊的：‘我今天在你们面前受审，是为了死人复活的事’那一句话。"
verses.textZhCuv: 纵然有，也不过一句话，就是我站在他们中间大声说：『我今日在你们面前受审，是为死人复活的道理。』」
verses.textEnNiv: unless it was this one thing I shouted as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’ "
verses.textEnEsv: other than this one thing that I cried out while standing among them: ‘It is with respect to the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you this day.’"
verses.textEnNkjv: Or else let those who are here themselves say if they found any wrongdoing in me while I stood before the council,
verses.textEnNlt: except for the one time I shouted out, ‘I am on trial before you today because I believe in the resurrection of the dead!’"
verses.textEnNasb: other than in regard to this one declaration which I shouted while standing among them, ‘For the resurrection of the dead I am on trial before you today!’ "
verses.textEn: unless it was this one thing I shouted as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’ "

verses.textZh: 腓力斯本来就详细晓得这道，却故意拖延他们，说："等千夫长吕西亚来了，再断定你们的事。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 腓力斯本来就详细晓得这道，却故意拖延他们，说："等千夫长吕西亚来了，再断定你们的事。"
verses.textZhCuv: 腓力斯本是详细晓得这道，就支吾他们说：「且等千夫长吕西亚下来，我要审断你们的事。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Felix, who was well acquainted with the Way, adjourned the proceedings. "When Lysias the commander comes," he said, "I will decide your case."
verses.textEnEsv: But Felix, having a rather accurate knowledge of the Way, put them off, saying, "When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will decide your case."
verses.textEnNkjv: unless itis for this one statement which I cried out, standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged by you this day.’ "
verses.textEnNlt: At that point Felix, who was quite familiar with the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, "Wait until Lysias, the garrison commander, arrives. Then I will decide the case."
verses.textEnNasb: But Felix, having quite accurate knowledge about the Way, adjourned them, saying, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case."
verses.textEn: Then Felix, who was well acquainted with the Way, adjourned the proceedings. "When Lysias the commander comes," he said, "I will decide your case."

verses.textZh: 于是吩咐百夫长看守保罗，但要宽待他，不可阻止亲友来照料他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是吩咐百夫长看守保罗，但要宽待他，不可阻止亲友来照料他。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是吩咐百夫长看守保罗，并且宽待他，也不拦阻他的亲友来供给他。
verses.textEnNiv: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard but to give him some freedom and permit his friends to take care of his needs.
verses.textEnEsv: Then he gave orders to the centurion that he should be kept in custody but have some liberty, and that none of his friends should be prevented from attending to his needs.
verses.textEnNkjv: But when Felix heard these things, having more accurate knowledge of the Way, he adjourned the proceedings and said, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will make a decision on your case."
verses.textEnNlt: He ordered an officer to keep Paul in custody but to give him some freedom and allow his friends to visit him and take care of his needs.
verses.textEnNasb: He gave orders to the centurion for Paul to be kept in custody and yet have some freedom, and not to prevent any of his friends from providing for his needs.
verses.textEn: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard but to give him some freedom and permit his friends to take care of his needs.

verses.textZh: 过了几天，腓力斯和他的犹太妻子土西拉一同来到，他又传见保罗，听他谈论在耶稣基督里的信仰。
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了几天，腓力斯和他的犹太妻子土西拉一同来到，他又传见保罗，听他谈论在耶稣基督里的信仰。
verses.textZhCuv: 过了几天，腓力斯和他夫人－犹太的女子土西拉－一同来到，就叫了保罗来，听他讲论信基督耶稣的道。
verses.textEnNiv: Several days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and listened to him as he spoke about faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.textEnEsv: After some days Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and he sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.textEnNkjv: So he commanded the centurion to keep Paul and to let him have liberty, and told him not to forbid any of his friends to provide for or visit him.
verses.textEnNlt: A few days later Felix came back with his wife, Drusilla, who was Jewish. Sending for Paul, they listened as he told them about faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.textEnNasb: Now some days later Felix arrived with Drusilla his wife, who was Jewish, and he sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.textEn: Several days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and listened to him as he spoke about faith in Christ Jesus.

verses.textZh: 保罗讲到公义、自制和将来的审判的时候，腓力斯就害怕起来，说："你先走吧，等我有空的时候再叫你来。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗讲到公义、自制和将来的审判的时候，腓力斯就害怕起来，说："你先走吧，等我有空的时候再叫你来。"
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗讲论公义、节制，和将来的审判。腓力斯甚觉恐惧，说：「你暂且去吧，等我得便再叫你来。」
verses.textEnNiv: As Paul talked about righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and said, "That’s enough for now! You may leave. When I find it convenient, I will send for you."
verses.textEnEsv: And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix was alarmed and said, "Go away for the present. When I get an opportunity I will summon you."
verses.textEnNkjv: And after some days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
verses.textEnNlt: As he reasoned with them about righteousness and self-control and the coming day of judgment, Felix became frightened. "Go away for now," he replied. "When it is more convenient, I’ll call for you again."
verses.textEnNasb: But as he was discussing righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix became frightened and responded, "Go away for now, and when I have an opportunity, I will summon you."
verses.textEn: As Paul talked about righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and said, "That’s enough for now! You may leave. When I find it convenient, I will send for you."

verses.textZh: 同时他也希望保罗送钱给他，所以又多次传见他，和他谈话。
verses.textZhCnvs: 同时他也希望保罗送钱给他，所以又多次传见他，和他谈话。
verses.textZhCuv: 腓力斯又指望保罗送他银钱，所以屡次叫他来，和他谈论。
verses.textEnNiv: At the same time he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe, so he sent for him frequently and talked with him.
verses.textEnEsv: At the same time he hoped that money would be given him by Paul. So he sent for him often and conversed with him.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, "Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you."
verses.textEnNlt: He also hoped that Paul would bribe him, so he sent for him quite often and talked with him.
verses.textEnNasb: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul; therefore he also used to send for him quite often and talk with him.
verses.textEn: At the same time he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe, so he sent for him frequently and talked with him.

verses.textZh: 过了两年，波求．非斯都接了腓力斯的任；腓力斯为要讨好犹太人，就把保罗留在监里。
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了两年，波求．非斯都接了腓力斯的任；腓力斯为要讨好犹太人，就把保罗留在监里。
verses.textZhCuv: 过了两年，波求‧非斯都接了腓力斯的任；腓力斯要讨犹太人的喜欢，就留保罗在监里。
verses.textEnNiv: When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, but because Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.
verses.textEnEsv: When two years had elapsed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And desiring to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
verses.textEnNkjv: Meanwhile he also hoped that money would be given him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore he sent for him more often and conversed with him.
verses.textEnNlt: After two years went by in this way, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And because Felix wanted to gain favor with the Jewish people, he left Paul in prison.
verses.textEnNasb: But after two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus; and Felix, wanting to do the Jews a favor, left Paul imprisoned.
verses.textEn: When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, but because Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.

verses.textZh: 非斯都到任三天之后，就从该撒利亚去耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCnvs: 非斯都到任三天之后，就从该撒利亚去耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCuv: 非斯都到了任，过了三天，就从凯撒利亚上耶路撒冷去。
verses.textEnNiv: Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,
verses.textEnEsv: Now three days after Festus had arrived in the province, he went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now when Festus had come to the province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNlt: Three days after Festus arrived in Caesarea to take over his new responsibilities, he left for Jerusalem,
verses.textEnNasb: Festus, then, after arriving in the province, went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea three days later.
verses.textEn: Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,

verses.textZh: 祭司长和犹太人的首领，到他面前控告保罗。他们又要求非斯都，
verses.textZhCnvs: 祭司长和犹太人的首领，到他面前控告保罗。他们又要求非斯都，
verses.textZhCuv: 祭司长和犹太人的首领向他控告保罗，
verses.textEnNiv: where the chief priests and the Jewish leaders appeared before him and presented the charges against Paul.
verses.textEnEsv: And the chief priests and the principal men of the Jews laid out their case against Paul, and they urged him,
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the high priest and the chief men of the Jews informed him against Paul; and they petitioned him,
verses.textEnNlt: where the leading priests and other Jewish leaders met with him and made their accusations against Paul.
verses.textEnNasb: And the chief priests and the leading men of the Jews brought charges against Paul, and they were pleading with Festus,
verses.textEn: where the chief priests and the Jewish leaders appeared before him and presented the charges against Paul.

verses.textZh: 求他恩准对付保罗，把保罗解来耶路撒冷，他们好埋伏在路上杀死他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 求他恩准对付保罗，把保罗解来耶路撒冷，他们好埋伏在路上杀死他。
verses.textZhCuv: 又央告他，求他的情，将保罗提到耶路撒冷来，他们要在路上埋伏杀害他。
verses.textEnNiv: They requested Festus, as a favor to them, to have Paul transferred to Jerusalem, for they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
verses.textEnEsv: asking as a favor against Paul that he summon him to Jerusalem—because they were planning an ambush to kill him on the way.
verses.textEnNkjv: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem— while they lay in ambush along the road to kill him.
verses.textEnNlt: They asked Festus as a favor to transfer Paul to Jerusalem (planning to ambush and kill him on the way).
verses.textEnNasb: requesting a concession against Paul, that he might have him brought to Jerusalem (at the same time, setting an ambush to kill him on the way).
verses.textEn: They requested Festus, as a favor to them, to have Paul transferred to Jerusalem, for they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.

verses.textZh: 非斯都回答："保罗现今押在该撒利亚，我就要回到那里去。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 非斯都回答："保罗现今押在该撒利亚，我就要回到那里去。"
verses.textZhCuv: 非斯都却回答说：「保罗押在凯撒利亚，我自己快要往那里去」；
verses.textEnNiv: Festus answered, "Paul is being held at Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.
verses.textEnEsv: Festus replied that Paul was being kept at Caesarea and that he himself intended to go there shortly.
verses.textEnNkjv: But Festus answered that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself was going there shortly.
verses.textEnNlt: But Festus replied that Paul was at Caesarea and he himself would be returning there soon.
verses.textEnNasb: Festus then answered that Paul was being kept in custody in Caesarea, and that he himself was about to leave shortly.
verses.textEn: Festus answered, "Paul is being held at Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.

verses.textZh: 又说："你们中间有权势的，和我一同去吧！那人若有甚么不是，他们就可以告他。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 又说："你们中间有权势的，和我一同去吧！那人若有甚么不是，他们就可以告他。"
verses.textZhCuv: 又说：「你们中间有权势的人与我一同下去，那人若有什么不是，就可以告他。」
verses.textEnNiv: Let some of your leaders come with me, and if the man has done anything wrong, they can press charges against him there."
verses.textEnEsv: "So," said he, "let the men of authority among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong about the man, let them bring charges against him."
verses.textEnNkjv: "Therefore," he said, "let those who have authority among you go down with me and accuse this man, to see if there is any fault in him."
verses.textEnNlt: So he said, "Those of you in authority can return with me. If Paul has done anything wrong, you can make your accusations."
verses.textEnNasb: "Therefore," he *said, "have the influential men among you go there with me, and if there is anything wrong about the man, have them bring charges against him."
verses.textEn: Let some of your leaders come with me, and if the man has done anything wrong, they can press charges against him there."

verses.textZh: 非斯都在他们那里大约逗留了不过十天八天，就回到该撒利亚去。第二天就开庭，吩咐把保罗带来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 非斯都在他们那里大约逗留了不过十天八天，就回到该撒利亚去。第二天就开庭，吩咐把保罗带来。
verses.textZhCuv: 非斯都在他们那里住了不过十天八天，就下凯撒利亚去；第二天坐堂，吩咐将保罗提上来。
verses.textEnNiv: After spending eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he convened the court and ordered that Paul be brought before him.
verses.textEnEsv: After he stayed among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea. And the next day he took his seat on the tribunal and ordered Paul to be brought.
verses.textEnNkjv: And when he had remained among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea. And the next day, sitting on the judgment seat, he commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.textEnNlt: About eight or ten days later Festus returned to Caesarea, and on the following day he took his seat in court and ordered that Paul be brought in.
verses.textEnNasb: After Festus had spent no more than eight or ten days among them, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he took his seat on the tribunal and ordered that Paul be brought.
verses.textEn: After spending eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he convened the court and ordered that Paul be brought before him.

verses.textZh: 保罗一到，那些从耶路撒冷来的犹太人，就站在他周围，提出许多严重的控告，可是所控告的他们都不能证实。
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗一到，那些从耶路撒冷来的犹太人，就站在他周围，提出许多严重的控告，可是所控告的他们都不能证实。
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗来了，那些从耶路撒冷下来的犹太人周围站着，将许多重大的事控告他，都是不能证实的。
verses.textEnNiv: When Paul came in, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him. They brought many serious charges against him, but they could not prove them.
verses.textEnEsv: When he had arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many and serious charges against him that they could not prove.
verses.textEnNkjv: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood about and laid many serious complaints against Paul, which they could not prove,
verses.textEnNlt: When Paul arrived, the Jewish leaders from Jerusalem gathered around and made many serious accusations they couldn’t prove.
verses.textEnNasb: After Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many, and serious, charges against him which they could not prove,
verses.textEn: When Paul came in, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him. They brought many serious charges against him, but they could not prove them.

verses.textZh: 保罗申辩说："无论对犹太人的律法、圣殿或凯撒，我都没有罪。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗申辩说："无论对犹太人的律法、圣殿或凯撒，我都没有罪。"
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗分诉说：「无论犹太人的律法，或是圣殿，或是凯撒，我都没有干犯。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Paul made his defense: "I have done nothing wrong against the Jewish law or against the temple or against Caesar."
verses.textEnEsv: Paul argued in his defense, "Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I committed any offense."
verses.textEnNkjv: while he answered for himself, "Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I offended in anything at all."
verses.textEnNlt: Paul denied the charges. "I am not guilty of any crime against the Jewish laws or the Temple or the Roman government," he said.
verses.textEnNasb: while Paul said in his own defense, "I have not done anything wrong either against the Law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against Caesar."
verses.textEn: Then Paul made his defense: "I have done nothing wrong against the Jewish law or against the temple or against Caesar."

verses.textZh: 但非斯都为要讨好犹太人，就问保罗："你愿意去耶路撒冷，让我在那里审问这事吗？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 但非斯都为要讨好犹太人，就问保罗："你愿意去耶路撒冷，让我在那里审问这事吗？"
verses.textZhCuv: 但非斯都要讨犹太人的喜欢，就问保罗说：「你愿意上耶路撒冷去，在那里听我审断这事吗？」
verses.textEnNiv: Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and stand trial before me there on these charges?"
verses.textEnEsv: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, "Do you wish to go up to Jerusalem and there be tried on these charges before me?"
verses.textEnNkjv: But Festus, wanting to do the Jews a favor, answered Paul and said, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and there be judged before me concerning these things?"
verses.textEnNlt: Then Festus, wanting to please the Jews, asked him, "Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial before me there?"
verses.textEnNasb: But Festus, wanting to do the Jews a favor, replied to Paul and said, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and stand trial before me on these charges?"
verses.textEn: Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and stand trial before me there on these charges?"

verses.textZh: 保罗说："我现在站在凯撒的审判台前，这里是我应当受审的地方。我对犹太人并没有作过甚么不对的事，这是你清楚知道的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗说："我现在站在凯撒的审判台前，这里是我应当受审的地方。我对犹太人并没有作过甚么不对的事，这是你清楚知道的。
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗说：「我站在凯撒的堂前，这就是我应当受审的地方。我向犹太人并没有行过什么不义的事，这也是你明明知道的。
verses.textEnNiv: Paul answered: "I am now standing before Caesar’s court, where I ought to be tried. I have not done any wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
verses.textEnEsv: But Paul said, "I am standing before Caesar’s tribunal, where I ought to be tried. To the Jews I have done no wrong, as you yourself know very well.
verses.textEnNkjv: So Paul said, "I stand at Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no wrong, as you very well know.
verses.textEnNlt: But Paul replied, "No! This is the official Roman court, so I ought to be tried right here. You know very well I am not guilty of harming the Jews.
verses.textEnNasb: But Paul said, "I am standing before Caesar’s tribunal, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you also very well know.
verses.textEn: Paul answered: "I am now standing before Caesar’s court, where I ought to be tried. I have not done any wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.

verses.textZh: 我若作过不对的事，犯过甚么该死的罪，就是死我也不推辞。不过，如果这些人告我的事不是真的，谁也不可以把我送给他们。我要向凯撒上诉。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 我若作过不对的事，犯过甚么该死的罪，就是死我也不推辞。不过，如果这些人告我的事不是真的，谁也不可以把我送给他们。我要向凯撒上诉。"
verses.textZhCuv: 我若行了不义的事，犯了什么该死的罪，就是死，我也不辞。他们所告我的事若都不实，就没有人可以把我交给他们。我要上告于凯撒。」
verses.textEnNiv: If, however, I am guilty of doing anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if the charges brought against me by these Jews are not true, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!"
verses.textEnEsv: If then I am a wrongdoer and have committed anything for which I deserve to die, I do not seek to escape death. But if there is nothing to their charges against me, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar."
verses.textEnNkjv: For if I am an offender, or have committed anything deserving of death, I do not object to dying; but if there is nothing in these things of which these men accuse me, no one can deliver me to them. I appeal to Caesar."
verses.textEnNlt: If I have done something worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die. But if I am innocent, no one has a right to turn me over to these men to kill me. I appeal to Caesar!"
verses.textEnNasb: If, therefore, I am in the wrong and have committed something deserving death, I am not trying to avoid execution; but if there is nothing to the accusations which these men are bringing against me, no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar."
verses.textEn: If, however, I am guilty of doing anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if the charges brought against me by these Jews are not true, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!"

verses.textZh: 非斯都同议会商量后，答复说："你既然要向凯撒上诉，可以到凯撒那里去。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 非斯都同议会商量后，答复说："你既然要向凯撒上诉，可以到凯撒那里去。"
verses.textZhCuv: 非斯都和议会商量了，就说：「你既上告于凯撒，可以往凯撒那里去。」
verses.textEnNiv: After Festus had conferred with his council, he declared: "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!"
verses.textEnEsv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with his council, answered, "To Caesar you have appealed; to Caesar you shall go."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, "You have appealed to Caesar? To Caesar you shall go!"
verses.textEnNlt: Festus conferred with his advisers and then replied, "Very well! You have appealed to Caesar, and to Caesar you will go!"
verses.textEnNasb: Then when Festus had conferred with his council, he answered, "You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go."
verses.textEn: After Festus had conferred with his council, he declared: "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!"

verses.textZh: 过了一些日子，亚基帕王和百尼基到该撒利亚来，问候非斯都。
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了一些日子，亚基帕王和百尼基到该撒利亚来，问候非斯都。
verses.textZhCuv: 过了些日子，亚基帕王和百妮基氏来到凯撒利亚，问非斯都安。
verses.textEnNiv: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
verses.textEnEsv: Now when some days had passed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
verses.textEnNkjv: And after some days King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.
verses.textEnNlt: A few days later King Agrippa arrived with his sister, Bernice, to pay their respects to Festus.
verses.textEnNasb: Now when several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived in Caesarea, paying their respects to Festus.
verses.textEn: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

verses.textZh: 他们在那里逗留了许多天，非斯都把保罗的案情向王陈明，说："这里有一个囚犯，是腓力斯留下来的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们在那里逗留了许多天，非斯都把保罗的案情向王陈明，说："这里有一个囚犯，是腓力斯留下来的。
verses.textZhCuv: 在那里住了多日，非斯都将保罗的事告诉王，说：「这里有一个人，是腓力斯留在监里的。
verses.textEnNiv: Since they were spending many days there, Festus discussed Paul’s case with the king. He said: "There is a man here whom Felix left as a prisoner.
verses.textEnEsv: And as they stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, "There is a man left prisoner by Felix,
verses.textEnNkjv: When they had been there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying: "There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix,
verses.textEnNlt: During their stay of several days, Festus discussed Paul’s case with the king. "There is a prisoner here," he told him, "whose case was left for me by Felix.
verses.textEnNasb: And while they were spending many days there, Festus presented Paul’s case to the king, saying, "There is a man who was left as a prisoner by Felix;
verses.textEn: Since they were spending many days there, Festus discussed Paul’s case with the king. He said: "There is a man here whom Felix left as a prisoner.

verses.textZh: 我在耶路撒冷的时候，祭司长和犹太人的长老控告他，要求把他定罪。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我在耶路撒冷的时候，祭司长和犹太人的长老控告他，要求把他定罪。
verses.textZhCuv: 我在耶路撒冷的时候，祭司长和犹太的长老将他的事禀报了我，求我定他的罪。
verses.textEnNiv: When I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges against him and asked that he be condemned.
verses.textEnEsv: and when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews laid out their case against him, asking for a sentence of condemnation against him.
verses.textEnNkjv: about whom the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, when I was in Jerusalem, asking for a judgment against him.
verses.textEnNlt: When I was in Jerusalem, the leading priests and Jewish elders pressed charges against him and asked me to condemn him.
verses.textEnNasb: and when I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges against him, asking for a sentence of condemnation against him.
verses.textEn: When I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges against him and asked that he be condemned.

verses.textZh: 我答复他们说，被告还没有和原告当面对证，又没有机会为所控的罪申辩，就被送给对方，罗马人没有这个规例。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我答复他们说，被告还没有和原告当面对证，又没有机会为所控的罪申辩，就被送给对方，罗马人没有这个规例。
verses.textZhCuv: 我对他们说，无论什么人，被告还没有和原告对质，未得机会分诉所告他的事，就先定他的罪，这不是罗马人的条例。
verses.textEnNiv: "I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand over anyone before they have faced their accusers and have had an opportunity to defend themselves against the charges.
verses.textEnEsv: I answered them that it was not the custom of the Romans to give up anyone before the accused met the accusers face to face and had opportunity to make his defense concerning the charge laid against him.
verses.textEnNkjv: To them I answered, ‘It is not the custom of the Romans to deliver any man to destruction before the accused meets the accusers face to face, and has opportunity to answer for himself concerning the charge against him.’
verses.textEnNlt: I pointed out to them that Roman law does not convict people without a trial. They must be given an opportunity to confront their accusers and defend themselves.
verses.textEnNasb: I replied to them that it is not the custom of the Romans to hand over any person before the accused meets his accusers face to face, and has an opportunity to make his defense against the charges.
verses.textEn: "I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand over anyone before they have faced their accusers and have had an opportunity to defend themselves against the charges.

verses.textZh: 后来他们都到了这里，我没有耽延时间，第二天就开庭，吩咐把那人提出来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 后来他们都到了这里，我没有耽延时间，第二天就开庭，吩咐把那人提出来。
verses.textZhCuv: 及至他们都来到这里，我就不耽延，第二天便坐堂，吩咐把那人提上来。
verses.textEnNiv: When they came here with me, I did not delay the case, but convened the court the next day and ordered the man to be brought in.
verses.textEnEsv: So when they came together here, I made no delay, but on the next day took my seat on the tribunal and ordered the man to be brought.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore when they had come together, without any delay, the next day I sat on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought in.
verses.textEnNlt: "When his accusers came here for the trial, I didn’t delay. I called the case the very next day and ordered Paul brought in.
verses.textEnNasb: So after they had assembled here, I did not delay, but on the next day took my seat on the tribunal and ordered that the man be brought.
verses.textEn: When they came here with me, I did not delay the case, but convened the court the next day and ordered the man to be brought in.

verses.textZh: 原告都站在那里，他们所控诉他的，并不是我所意料的恶事。
verses.textZhCnvs: 原告都站在那里，他们所控诉他的，并不是我所意料的恶事。
verses.textZhCuv: 告他的人站着告他；所告的，并没有我所逆料的那等恶事。
verses.textEnNiv: When his accusers got up to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.
verses.textEnEsv: When the accusers stood up, they brought no charge in his case of such evils as I supposed.
verses.textEnNkjv: When the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation against him of such things as I supposed,
verses.textEnNlt: But the accusations made against him weren’t any of the crimes I expected.
verses.textEnNasb: When the accusers stood up, they did not begin bringing any charges against him of crimes that I suspected,
verses.textEn: When his accusers got up to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.

verses.textZh: 他们与他争辩的，只是他们的宗教问题；还论到一位已经死了的耶稣，保罗却说他是活着的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们与他争辩的，只是他们的宗教问题；还论到一位已经死了的耶稣，保罗却说他是活着的。
verses.textZhCuv: 不过是有几样辩论，为他们自己敬鬼神的事，又为一个人名叫耶稣，是已经死了，保罗却说他是活着的。
verses.textEnNiv: Instead, they had some points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus who Paul claimed was alive.
verses.textEnEsv: Rather they had certain points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who was dead, but whom Paul asserted to be alive.
verses.textEnNkjv: but had some questions against him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.textEnNlt: Instead, it was something about their religion and a dead man named Jesus, who Paul insists is alive.
verses.textEnNasb: but they simply had some points of disagreement with him about their own religion and about a dead man, Jesus, whom Paul asserted to be alive.
verses.textEn: Instead, they had some points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus who Paul claimed was alive.

verses.textZh: 关于这些争论，我不知道怎样处理，就问他愿不愿意上耶路撒冷去为这些事在那里受审。
verses.textZhCnvs: 关于这些争论，我不知道怎样处理，就问他愿不愿意上耶路撒冷去为这些事在那里受审。
verses.textZhCuv: 这些事当怎样究问，我心里作难，所以问他说：『你愿意上耶路撒冷去，在那里为这些事听审吗？』
verses.textEnNiv: I was at a loss how to investigate such matters; so I asked if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial there on these charges.
verses.textEnEsv: Being at a loss how to investigate these questions, I asked whether he wanted to go to Jerusalem and be tried there regarding them.
verses.textEnNkjv: And because I was uncertain of such questions, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.
verses.textEnNlt: I was at a loss to know how to investigate these things, so I asked him whether he would be willing to stand trial on these charges in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: And being at a loss how to investigate such matters, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial there on these matters.
verses.textEn: I was at a loss how to investigate such matters; so I asked if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial there on these charges.

verses.textZh: 但保罗要求把他留下，等待皇上裁判，我就下令把他押起来，等候解往凯撒那里。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 但保罗要求把他留下，等待皇上裁判，我就下令把他押起来，等候解往凯撒那里。"
verses.textZhCuv: 但保罗求我留下他，要听皇上审断，我就吩咐把他留下，等我解他到凯撒那里去。」
verses.textEnNiv: But when Paul made his appeal to be held over for the Emperor’s decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar."
verses.textEnEsv: But when Paul had appealed to be kept in custody for the decision of the emperor, I ordered him to be held until I could send him to Caesar."
verses.textEnNkjv: But when Paul appealed to be reserved for the decision of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I could send him to Caesar."
verses.textEnNlt: But Paul appealed to have his case decided by the emperor. So I ordered that he be held in custody until I could arrange to send him to Caesar."
verses.textEnNasb: But when Paul appealed to be held in custody for the Emperor’s decision, I ordered that he be kept in custody until I send him to Caesar."
verses.textEn: But when Paul made his appeal to be held over for the Emperor’s decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar."

verses.textZh: 亚基帕对非斯都说："我也想听听这人说些甚么。"非斯都说："明天就请你来听。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 亚基帕对非斯都说："我也想听听这人说些甚么。"非斯都说："明天就请你来听。"
verses.textZhCuv: 亚基帕对非斯都说：「我自己也愿听这人辩论。」非斯都说：「明天你可以听。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear this man myself." He replied, "Tomorrow you will hear him."
verses.textEnEsv: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear the man myself." "Tomorrow," said he, "you will hear him."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I also would like to hear the man myself." "Tomorrow," he said, "you shall hear him."
verses.textEnNlt: "I’d like to hear the man myself," Agrippa said. And Festus replied, "You will—tomorrow!"
verses.textEnNasb: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I also would like to hear the man myself." "Tomorrow," he *said, "you shall hear him."
verses.textEn: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear this man myself." He replied, "Tomorrow you will hear him."

verses.textZh: 第二天，亚基帕和百尼基威风凛凛地来了，同千夫长和城中的显要进了厅堂。非斯都吩咐一声，就有人把保罗提出来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 第二天，亚基帕和百尼基威风凛凛地来了，同千夫长和城中的显要进了厅堂。非斯都吩咐一声，就有人把保罗提出来。
verses.textZhCuv: 第二天，亚基帕和百妮基大张威势而来，同着众千夫长和城里的尊贵人进了公厅。非斯都吩咐一声，就有人将保罗带进来。
verses.textEnNiv: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience room with the high-ranking military officers and the prominent men of the city. At the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
verses.textEnEsv: So on the next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp, and they entered the audience hall with the military tribunes and the prominent men of the city. Then, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
verses.textEnNkjv: So the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and had entered the auditorium with the commanders and the prominent men of the city, at Festus’ command Paul was brought in.
verses.textEnNlt: So the next day Agrippa and Bernice arrived at the auditorium with great pomp, accompanied by military officers and prominent men of the city. Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.
verses.textEnNasb: So, on the next day when Agrippa and Bernice came amid great pomp and entered the auditorium, accompanied by the commanders and the prominent men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought before them.
verses.textEn: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience room with the high-ranking military officers and the prominent men of the city. At the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

verses.textZh: 非斯都说："亚基帕王和在座的各位，请看这个人。耶路撒冷和本地的犹太人都向我请求，嚷着说这个人不该活着。
verses.textZhCnvs: 非斯都说："亚基帕王和在座的各位，请看这个人。耶路撒冷和本地的犹太人都向我请求，嚷着说这个人不该活着。
verses.textZhCuv: 非斯都说：「亚基帕王和在这里的诸位啊，你们看这人，就是一切犹太人，在耶路撒冷和这里，曾向我恳求、呼叫说：『不可容他再活着。』
verses.textEnNiv: Festus said: "King Agrippa, and all who are present with us, you see this man! The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him in Jerusalem and here in Caesarea, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.textEnEsv: And Festus said, "King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man about whom the whole Jewish people petitioned me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.textEnNkjv: And Festus said: "King Agrippa and all the men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom the whole assembly of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying out that he was not fit to live any longer.
verses.textEnNlt: Then Festus said, "King Agrippa and all who are here, this is the man whose death is demanded by all the Jews, both here and in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: And Festus *said, "King Agrippa, and all you gentlemen present with us, you see this man about whom all the people of the Jews appealed to me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.textEn: Festus said: "King Agrippa, and all who are present with us, you see this man! The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him in Jerusalem and here in Caesarea, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.

verses.textZh: 我查明他没有犯甚么该死的罪，但是他自己既然要向皇上上诉，我就决定把他解去。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我查明他没有犯甚么该死的罪，但是他自己既然要向皇上上诉，我就决定把他解去。
verses.textZhCuv: 但我查明他没有犯什么该死的罪，并且他自己上告于皇帝，所以我定意把他解去。
verses.textEnNiv: I found he had done nothing deserving of death, but because he made his appeal to the Emperor I decided to send him to Rome.
verses.textEnEsv: But I found that he had done nothing deserving death. And as he himself appealed to the emperor, I decided to go ahead and send him.
verses.textEnNkjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing deserving of death, and that he himself had appealed to Augustus, I decided to send him.
verses.textEnNlt: But in my opinion he has done nothing deserving death. However, since he appealed his case to the emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
verses.textEnNasb: But I found that he had committed nothing deserving death; and since he himself appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
verses.textEn: I found he had done nothing deserving of death, but because he made his appeal to the Emperor I decided to send him to Rome.

verses.textZh: 关于这个人，我没有甚么确实的事可以呈奏主上的。所以把他带到你们面前，特别是你亚基帕王面前，为要在审查之后，有所陈奏。
verses.textZhCnvs: 关于这个人，我没有甚么确实的事可以呈奏主上的。所以把他带到你们面前，特别是你亚基帕王面前，为要在审查之后，有所陈奏。
verses.textZhCuv: 论到这人，我没有确实的事可以奏明主上。因此，我带他到你们面前，也特意带他到你亚基帕王面前，为要在查问之后有所陈奏。
verses.textEnNiv: But I have nothing definite to write to His Majesty about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that as a result of this investigation I may have something to write.
verses.textEnEsv: But I have nothing definite to write to my lord about him. Therefore I have brought him before you all, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that, after we have examined him, I may have something to write.
verses.textEnNkjv: I have nothing certain to write to my lord concerning him. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the examination has taken place I may have something to write.
verses.textEnNlt: "But what shall I write the emperor? For there is no clear charge against him. So I have brought him before all of you, and especially you, King Agrippa, so that after we examine him, I might have something to write.
verses.textEnNasb: Yet, I have nothing definite about him to write to my lord. Therefore, I have brought him before you all and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the investigation has taken place, I may have something to write.
verses.textEn: But I have nothing definite to write to His Majesty about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that as a result of this investigation I may have something to write.

verses.textZh: 因为我认为解送囚犯，不指明他的罪状，是不合理的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为我认为解送囚犯，不指明他的罪状，是不合理的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 据我看来，解送囚犯，不指明他的罪案是不合理的。」
verses.textEnNiv: For I think it is unreasonable to send a prisoner on to Rome without specifying the charges against him."
verses.textEnEsv: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to indicate the charges against him."
verses.textEnNkjv: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner and not to specify the charges against him."
verses.textEnNlt: For it makes no sense to send a prisoner to the emperor without specifying the charges against him!"
verses.textEnNasb: For it seems absurd to me in sending a prisoner, not to indicate the charges against him as well."
verses.textEn: For I think it is unreasonable to send a prisoner on to Rome without specifying the charges against him."

verses.textZh: "亚基帕王啊，犹太人控告我的事，今天我可以在你面前辩护，实在是万幸；
verses.textZhCnvs: "亚基帕王啊，犹太人控告我的事，今天我可以在你面前辩护，实在是万幸；
verses.textZhCuv: 亚基帕王啊，犹太人所告我的一切事，今日得在你面前分诉，实为万幸；

verses.textEnEsv: "I consider myself fortunate that it is before you, King Agrippa, I am going to make my defense today against all the accusations of the Jews,

verses.textEnNiv: and especially so because you are well acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. Therefore, I beg you to listen to me patiently.
verses.textEnEsv: especially because you are familiar with all the customs and controversies of the Jews. Therefore I beg you to listen to me patiently.
verses.textEnNkjv: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which have to do with the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.
verses.textEnNlt: for I know you are an expert on all Jewish customs and controversies. Now please listen to me patiently!
verses.textEnNasb: especially because you are an expert in all customs and questions among the Jews; therefore I beg you to listen to me patiently.
verses.textEn: and especially so because you are well acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. Therefore, I beg you to listen to me patiently.

verses.textZh: 我从幼年到现在，在本国、在耶路撒冷为人怎样，犹太人都知道。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我从幼年到现在，在本国、在耶路撒冷为人怎样，犹太人都知道。
verses.textZhCuv: 我从起初在本国的民中，并在耶路撒冷，自幼为人如何，犹太人都知道。
verses.textEnNiv: "The Jewish people all know the way I have lived ever since I was a child, from the beginning of my life in my own country, and also in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnEsv: "My manner of life from my youth, spent from the beginning among my own nation and in Jerusalem, is known by all the Jews.
verses.textEnNkjv: "My manner of life from my youth, which was spent from the beginning among my own nation at Jerusalem, all the Jews know.
verses.textEnNlt: "As the Jewish leaders are well aware, I was given a thorough Jewish training from my earliest childhood among my own people and in Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: "So then, all Jews know my way of life since my youth, which from the beginning was spent among my own nation and in Jerusalem,
verses.textEn: "The Jewish people all know the way I have lived ever since I was a child, from the beginning of my life in my own country, and also in Jerusalem.

verses.textZh: 如果他们肯作证的话，他们是早就知道，我是按着我们祖宗最严格的教派，过着法利赛人的生活。
verses.textZhCnvs: 如果他们肯作证的话，他们是早就知道，我是按着我们祖宗最严格的教派，过着法利赛人的生活。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们若肯作见证就晓得，我从起初是按着我们教中最严紧的教门作了法利赛人。
verses.textEnNiv: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I conformed to the strictest sect of our religion, living as a Pharisee.
verses.textEnEsv: They have known for a long time, if they are willing to testify, that according to the strictest party of our religion I have lived as a Pharisee.
verses.textEnNkjv: They knew me from the first, if they were willing to testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.textEnNlt: If they would admit it, they know that I have been a member of the Pharisees, the strictest sect of our religion.
verses.textEnNasb: since they have known about me for a long time, if they are willing to testify, that I lived as a Pharisee according to the strictest sect of our religion.
verses.textEn: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I conformed to the strictest sect of our religion, living as a Pharisee.

verses.textZh: 现在我站着受审，是为了对神向我们祖先的应许存着盼望。
verses.textZhCnvs: 现在我站着受审，是为了对神向我们祖先的应许存着盼望。
verses.textZhCuv: 现在我站在这里受审，是因为指望神向我们祖宗所应许的；
verses.textEnNiv: And now it is because of my hope in what God has promised our ancestors that I am on trial today.
verses.textEnEsv: And now I stand here on trial because of my hope in the promise made by God to our fathers,
verses.textEnNkjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers.
verses.textEnNlt: Now I am on trial because of my hope in the fulfillment of God’s promise made to our ancestors.
verses.textEnNasb: And now I am standing trial for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers;
verses.textEn: And now it is because of my hope in what God has promised our ancestors that I am on trial today.

verses.textZh: 我们十二支派昼夜切切地事奉神，都是盼望这应许实现。王啊，我被犹太人控告，正是为了这个盼望。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们十二支派昼夜切切地事奉神，都是盼望这应许实现。王啊，我被犹太人控告，正是为了这个盼望。
verses.textZhCuv: 这应许，我们十二个支派，昼夜切切地事奉神，都指望得着。王啊，我被犹太人控告，就是因这指望。
verses.textEnNiv: This is the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. King Agrippa, it is because of this hope that these Jews are accusing me.
verses.textEnEsv: to which our twelve tribes hope to attain, as they earnestly worship night and day. And for this hope I am accused by Jews, O king!
verses.textEnNkjv: To this promise our twelve tribes, earnestly serving God night and day, hope to attain. For this hope’s sake, King Agrippa, I am accused by the Jews.
verses.textEnNlt: In fact, that is why the twelve tribes of Israel zealously worship God night and day, and they share the same hope I have. Yet, Your Majesty, they accuse me for having this hope!
verses.textEnNasb: the promise to which our twelve tribes hope to attain, as they earnestly serve God night and day. For this hope, O king, I am being accused by Jews.
verses.textEn: This is the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. King Agrippa, it is because of this hope that these Jews are accusing me.

verses.textZh: 神使死人复活，你们为甚么认为是不可信的呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 神使死人复活，你们为甚么认为是不可信的呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 神叫死人复活，你们为什么看作不可信的呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Why should any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
verses.textEnEsv: Why is it thought incredible by any of you that God raises the dead?
verses.textEnNkjv: Why should it be thought incredible by you that God raises the dead?
verses.textEnNlt: Why does it seem incredible to any of you that God can raise the dead?
verses.textEnNasb: Why is it considered incredible among you people if God raises the dead?
verses.textEn: Why should any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?

verses.textZh: 从前，我也认为应该多方敌对拿撒勒人耶稣的名。
verses.textZhCnvs: 从前，我也认为应该多方敌对拿撒勒人耶稣的名。
verses.textZhCuv: 从前我自己以为应当多方攻击拿撒勒人耶稣的名，
verses.textEnNiv: "I too was convinced that I ought to do all that was possible to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.textEnEsv: "I myself was convinced that I ought to do many things in opposing the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.textEnNkjv: "Indeed, I myself thought I must do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.textEnNlt: "I used to believe that I ought to do everything I could to oppose the very name of Jesus the Nazarene.
verses.textEnNasb: "So I thought to myself that I had to act in strong opposition to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.textEn: "I too was convinced that I ought to do all that was possible to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.textZh: 后来就在耶路撒冷这样作了。我得到了众祭司长授权，把许多圣徒关在监里，并且他们被杀的时候，我也表示同意。
verses.textZhCnvs: 后来就在耶路撒冷这样作了。我得到了众祭司长授权，把许多圣徒关在监里，并且他们被杀的时候，我也表示同意。
verses.textZhCuv: 我在耶路撒冷也曾这样行了。既从祭司长得了权柄，我就把许多圣徒囚在监里。他们被杀，我也出名定案。
verses.textEnNiv: And that is just what I did in Jerusalem. On the authority of the chief priests I put many of the Lord’s people in prison, and when they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.
verses.textEnEsv: And I did so in Jerusalem. I not only locked up many of the saints in prison after receiving authority from the chief priests, but when they were put to death I cast my vote against them.
verses.textEnNkjv: This I also did in Jerusalem, and many of the saints I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.
verses.textEnNlt: Indeed, I did just that in Jerusalem. Authorized by the leading priests, I caused many believers there to be sent to prison. And I cast my vote against them when they were condemned to death.
verses.textEnNasb: And this is just what I did in Jerusalem; not only did I lock up many of the saints in prisons, after receiving authority from the chief priests, but I also cast my vote against them when they were being put to death.
verses.textEn: And that is just what I did in Jerusalem. On the authority of the chief priests I put many of the Lord’s people in prison, and when they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.

verses.textZh: 我在各会堂里多次用刑强迫他们说亵渎的话；我非常愤恨他们，甚至追到国外的城巿去迫害他们。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我在各会堂里多次用刑强迫他们说亵渎的话；我非常愤恨他们，甚至追到国外的城巿去迫害他们。
verses.textZhCuv: 在各会堂，我屡次用刑强逼他们说亵渎的话，又分外恼恨他们，甚至追逼他们，直到外邦的城邑。」
verses.textEnNiv: Many a time I went from one synagogue to another to have them punished, and I tried to force them to blaspheme. I was so obsessed with persecuting them that I even hunted them down in foreign cities.
verses.textEnEsv: And I punished them often in all the synagogues and tried to make them blaspheme, and in raging fury against them I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
verses.textEnNkjv: And I punished them often in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
verses.textEnNlt: Many times I had them punished in the synagogues to get them to curse Jesus. I was so violently opposed to them that I even chased them down in foreign cities.
verses.textEnNasb: And as I punished them often in all the synagogues, I tried to force them to blaspheme; and since I was extremely enraged at them, I kept pursuing them even to foreign cities.
verses.textEn: Many a time I went from one synagogue to another to have them punished, and I tried to force them to blaspheme. I was so obsessed with persecuting them that I even hunted them down in foreign cities.

verses.textZh: "那时候，我得到祭司长的授权和准许，去大马士革。
verses.textZhCnvs: "那时候，我得到祭司长的授权和准许，去大马士革。
verses.textZhCuv: 「那时，我领了祭司长的权柄和命令，往大马士革去。
verses.textEnNiv: "On one of these journeys I was going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
verses.textEnEsv: "In this connection I journeyed to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
verses.textEnNkjv: "While thus occupied, as I journeyed to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.textEnNlt: "One day I was on such a mission to Damascus, armed with the authority and commission of the leading priests.
verses.textEnNasb: " While so engaged, as I was journeying to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests,
verses.textEn: "On one of these journeys I was going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

verses.textZh: 王啊，就在中午的时候，我在路上看见一道光，比太阳更明亮，从天上四面照着我和同行的人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王啊，就在中午的时候，我在路上看见一道光，比太阳更明亮，从天上四面照着我和同行的人。
verses.textZhCuv: 王啊，我在路上，晌午的时候，看见从天发光，比日头还亮，四面照着我并与我同行的人。
verses.textEnNiv: About noon, King Agrippa, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, blazing around me and my companions.
verses.textEnEsv: At midday, O king, I saw on the way a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, that shone around me and those who journeyed with me.
verses.textEnNkjv: at midday, O king, along the road I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who journeyed with me.
verses.textEnNlt: About noon, Your Majesty, as I was on the road, a light from heaven brighter than the sun shone down on me and my companions.
verses.textEnNasb: at midday, O king, I saw on the way a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who were journeying with me.
verses.textEn: About noon, King Agrippa, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, blazing around me and my companions.

verses.textZh: <red>我们都仆倒在地上，我听见有声音用希伯来话对我说：‘扫罗！扫罗！你为甚么迫害我？你要踢刺是难的。’</red>
verses.textZhCnvs: <red>我们都仆倒在地上，我听见有声音用希伯来话对我说：‘扫罗！扫罗！你为甚么迫害我？你要踢刺是难的。’</red>
verses.textZhCuv: <red>我们都仆倒在地，我就听见有声音用希伯来话向我说：『扫罗！扫罗！为什么逼迫我？你用脚踢刺是难的！』</red>
verses.textEnNiv: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me in Aramaic, <red>‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’</red>
verses.textEnEsv: And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
verses.textEnNkjv: And when we all had fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me and saying in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
verses.textEnNlt: We all fell down, and I heard a voice saying to me in Aramaic, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is useless for you to fight against my will. ’
verses.textEnNasb: And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew dialect, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
verses.textEn: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me in Aramaic, <red>‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’</red>

verses.textZh: <red>我说：‘主啊，你是谁？’主说：‘我就是你所迫害的耶稣。</red>
verses.textZhCnvs: <red>我说：‘主啊，你是谁？’主说：‘我就是你所迫害的耶稣。</red>
verses.textZhCuv: <red>我说：『主啊，你是谁？』主说：『我就是你所逼迫的耶稣。</red>
verses.textEnNiv: “Then I asked, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ <red>“‘Ip am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’</red> the Lord replied.
verses.textEnEsv: And I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ And the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus whom you are persecuting.
verses.textEnNkjv: So I said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.textEnNlt: "‘Who are you, lord?’ I asked. "And the Lord replied, ‘I am Jesus, the one you are persecuting.
verses.textEnNasb: And I said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus whom you are persecuting.
verses.textEn: “Then I asked, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ <red>“‘Ip am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’</red> the Lord replied.

verses.textZh: <red>你起来，站着，我向你显现，是要指派你为我工作。你要为你所见过的事，和我将要向你显明的事作见证。</red>
verses.textZhCnvs: <red>你起来，站着，我向你显现，是要指派你为我工作。你要为你所见过的事，和我将要向你显明的事作见证。</red>
verses.textZhCuv: <red>你起来站着，我特意向你显现，要派你作执事，作见证，将你所看见的事和我将要指示你的事证明出来。</red>
verses.textEnNiv: <red>‘Now get up and stand on your feet. I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen and will see of me.</red>
verses.textEnEsv: But rise and stand upon your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to appoint you as a servant and witness to the things in which you have seen me and to those in which I will appear to you,
verses.textEnNkjv: But rise and stand on your feet; for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of the things which you have seen and of the things which I will yet reveal to you.
verses.textEnNlt: Now get to your feet! For I have appeared to you to appoint you as my servant and witness. Tell people that you have seen me, and tell them what I will show you in the future.
verses.textEnNasb: But get up and stand on your feet; for this purpose I have appeared to you, to appoint you as a servant and a witness not only to the things in which you have seen Me, but also to the things in which I will appear to you,
verses.textEn: <red>‘Now get up and stand on your feet. I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen and will see of me.</red>

verses.textZh: <red>我要救你脱离这人民和外族人，差遣你到他们那里去，</red>
verses.textZhCnvs: <red>我要救你脱离这人民和外族人，差遣你到他们那里去，</red>
verses.textZhCuv: <red>我也要救你脱离百姓和外邦人的手。</red>
verses.textEnNiv: <red>I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them</red>
verses.textEnEsv: delivering you from your people and from the Gentiles— to whom I am sending you
verses.textEnNkjv: I will deliver you from the Jewish people, as well as from the Gentiles, to whom I now send you,
verses.textEnNlt: And I will rescue you from both your own people and the Gentiles. Yes, I am sending you to the Gentiles
verses.textEnNasb: rescuing you from the Jewish people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,
verses.textEn: <red>I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them</red>

verses.textZh: <red>开他们的眼睛，使他们从黑暗中归向光明，从撒但的权下归向神，使他们的罪恶得到赦免，并且在那些因信我而成圣的人中同得基业。’</red>
verses.textZhCnvs: <red>开他们的眼睛，使他们从黑暗中归向光明，从撒但的权下归向神，使他们的罪恶得到赦免，并且在那些因信我而成圣的人中同得基业。’</red>
verses.textZhCuv: <red>我差你到他们那里去，要叫他们的眼睛得开，从黑暗中归向光明，从撒但权下归向神；又因信我，得蒙赦罪，和一切成圣的人同得基业。』」</red>
verses.textEnNiv: <red>to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’</red>
verses.textEnEsv: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
verses.textEnNkjv: to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’
verses.textEnNlt: to open their eyes, so they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then they will receive forgiveness for their sins and be given a place among God’s people, who are set apart by faith in me.’
verses.textEnNasb: to open their eyes so that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who have been sanctified by faith in Me.’
verses.textEn: <red>to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’</red>

verses.textZh: "亚基帕王啊，因此，我没有违背这从天上来的异象，
verses.textZhCnvs: "亚基帕王啊，因此，我没有违背这从天上来的异象，
verses.textZhCuv: 「亚基帕王啊，我故此没有违背那从天上来的异象；
verses.textEnNiv: "So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the vision from heaven.
verses.textEnEsv: "Therefore, O King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
verses.textEnNkjv: "Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
verses.textEnNlt: "And so, King Agrippa, I obeyed that vision from heaven.
verses.textEnNasb: "For that reason, King Agrippa, I did not prove disobedient to the heavenly vision,
verses.textEn: "So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the vision from heaven.

verses.textZh: 先向大马士革、耶路撒冷、犹太全地的人宣讲，后向外族人宣讲，叫他们悔改，归向神，行事与悔改的心相称。
verses.textZhCnvs: 先向大马士革、耶路撒冷、犹太全地的人宣讲，后向外族人宣讲，叫他们悔改，归向神，行事与悔改的心相称。
verses.textZhCuv: 先在大马士革，后在耶路撒冷和犹太全地，以及外邦，劝勉他们应当悔改归向神，行事与悔改的心相称。
verses.textEnNiv: First to those in Damascus, then to those in Jerusalem and in all Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I preached that they should repent and turn to God and demonstrate their repentance by their deeds.
verses.textEnEsv: but declared first to those in Damascus, then in Jerusalem and throughout all the region of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds in keeping with their repentance.
verses.textEnNkjv: but declared first to those in Damascus and in Jerusalem, and throughout all the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent, turn to God, and do works befitting repentance.
verses.textEnNlt: I preached first to those in Damascus, then in Jerusalem and throughout all Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that all must repent of their sins and turn to God—and prove they have changed by the good things they do.
verses.textEnNasb: but continually proclaimed to those in Damascus first, and in Jerusalem, and then all the region of Judea, and even to the Gentiles, that they are to repent and turn to God, performing deeds consistent with repentance.
verses.textEn: First to those in Damascus, then to those in Jerusalem and in all Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I preached that they should repent and turn to God and demonstrate their repentance by their deeds.

verses.textZh: 犹太人就是为了这缘故在殿里捉住我，想要杀我。
verses.textZhCnvs: 犹太人就是为了这缘故在殿里捉住我，想要杀我。
verses.textZhCuv: 因此，犹太人在殿里拿住我，想要杀我。
verses.textEnNiv: That is why some Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
verses.textEnEsv: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
verses.textEnNkjv: For these reasons the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
verses.textEnNlt: Some Jews arrested me in the Temple for preaching this, and they tried to kill me.
verses.textEnNasb: For these reasons some Jews seized me in the temple and tried to murder me.
verses.textEn: That is why some Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.

verses.textZh: 然而，我得到神的帮助，直到今日还是站得稳，向尊卑老幼作见证，我所讲的都是众先知和摩西所论的将来必成的事，
verses.textZhCnvs: 然而，我得到神的帮助，直到今日还是站得稳，向尊卑老幼作见证，我所讲的都是众先知和摩西所论的将来必成的事，
verses.textZhCuv: 然而我蒙神的帮助，直到今日还站得住，对着尊贵、卑贱、老幼作见证；所讲的并不外乎众先知和摩西所说将来必成的事，
verses.textEnNiv: But God has helped me to this very day; so I stand here and testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen—
verses.textEnEsv: To this day I have had the help that comes from God, and so I stand here testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would come to pass:
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore, having obtained help from God, to this day I stand, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other things than those which the prophets and Moses said would come—
verses.textEnNlt: But God has protected me right up to this present time so I can testify to everyone, from the least to the greatest. I teach nothing except what the prophets and Moses said would happen—
verses.textEnNasb: So, having obtained help from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, stating nothing but what the Prophets and Moses said was going to take place,
verses.textEn: But God has helped me to this very day; so I stand here and testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen—

verses.textZhCnvs: 就是基督必须受难，并且从死人中首先复活，把光明的信息传报给这人民和外族人。"
verses.textZhCuv: 就是基督必须受害，并且因从死里复活，要首先把光明的道传给百姓和外邦人。」
verses.textEnNiv: that the Messiah would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, would bring the message of light to his own people and to the Gentiles."
verses.textEnEsv: that the Christ must suffer and that, by being the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles."
verses.textEnNkjv: that the Christ would suffer, that He would be the first to rise from the dead, and would proclaim light to the Jewish people and to the Gentiles."
verses.textEnNlt: that the Messiah would suffer and be the first to rise from the dead, and in this way announce God’s light to Jews and Gentiles alike."
verses.textEnNasb: as to whether the Christ was to suffer, and whether, as first from the resurrection of the dead, He would proclaim light both to the Jewish people and to the Gentiles."
verses.textEn: that the Messiah would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, would bring the message of light to his own people and to the Gentiles."

verses.textZh: 保罗申诉到这里，非斯都大声说："保罗！你疯了；你的学问太大，使你疯了！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗申诉到这里，非斯都大声说："保罗！你疯了；你的学问太大，使你疯了！"
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗这样分诉，非斯都大声说：「保罗，你癫狂了吧。你的学问太大，反叫你癫狂了！」
verses.textEnNiv: At this point Festus interrupted Paul’s defense. "You are out of your mind, Paul!" he shouted. "Your great learning is driving you insane."
verses.textEnEsv: And as he was saying these things in his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, "Paul, you are out of your mind; your great learning is driving you out of your mind."
verses.textEnNkjv: Now as he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, "Paul, you are beside yourself! Much learning is driving you mad!"
verses.textEnNlt: Suddenly, Festus shouted, "Paul, you are insane. Too much study has made you crazy!"
verses.textEnNasb: While Paul was stating these things in his defense, Festus *said in a loud voice, "Paul, you are out of your mind! Your great learning is driving you insane."
verses.textEn: At this point Festus interrupted Paul’s defense. "You are out of your mind, Paul!" he shouted. "Your great learning is driving you insane."

verses.textZh: 保罗说："非斯都大人，我没有疯，我说的都是真实的话，清醒的话。
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗说："非斯都大人，我没有疯，我说的都是真实的话，清醒的话。
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗说：「非斯都大人，我不是癫狂，我说的乃是真实明白话。
verses.textEnNiv: "I am not insane, most excellent Festus," Paul replied. "What I am saying is true and reasonable.
verses.textEnEsv: But Paul said, "I am not out of my mind, most excellent Festus, but I am speaking true and rational words.
verses.textEnNkjv: But he said, "I am not mad, most noble Festus, but speak the words of truth and reason.
verses.textEnNlt: But Paul replied, "I am not insane, Most Excellent Festus. What I am saying is the sober truth.
verses.textEnNasb: But Paul *said, "I am not insane, most excellent Festus; on the contrary, I am speaking out with truthful and rational words.
verses.textEn: "I am not insane, most excellent Festus," Paul replied. "What I am saying is true and reasonable.

verses.textZh: 因为王知道这些事，所以我对王坦白直说。我确信这些事没有一件能瞒得过他，因为这不是在背地里作的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为王知道这些事，所以我对王坦白直说。我确信这些事没有一件能瞒得过他，因为这不是在背地里作的。
verses.textZhCuv: 王也晓得这些事，所以我向王放胆直言，我深信这些事没有一件向王隐藏的，因都不是在背地里做的。
verses.textEnNiv: The king is familiar with these things, and I can speak freely to him. I am convinced that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
verses.textEnEsv: For the king knows about these things, and to him I speak boldly. For I am persuaded that none of these things has escaped his notice, for this has not been done in a corner.
verses.textEnNkjv: For the king, before whom I also speak freely, knows these things; for I am convinced that none of these things escapes his attention, since this thing was not done in a corner.
verses.textEnNlt: And King Agrippa knows about these things. I speak boldly, for I am sure these events are all familiar to him, for they were not done in a corner!
verses.textEnNasb: For the king knows about these matters, and I also speak to him with confidence, since I am persuaded that none of these things escape his notice; for this has not been done in a corner.
verses.textEn: The king is familiar with these things, and I can speak freely to him. I am convinced that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.

verses.textZh: 亚基帕王啊，你信先知吗？我知道你是信的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 亚基帕王啊，你信先知吗？我知道你是信的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 亚基帕王啊，你信先知吗？我知道你是信的。」
verses.textEnNiv: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do."
verses.textEnEsv: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."
verses.textEnNkjv: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you do believe."
verses.textEnNlt: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do—"
verses.textEnNasb: King Agrippa, do you believe the Prophets? I know that you believe."
verses.textEn: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do."

verses.textZh: 亚基帕对保罗说："你想用这样短短的时间就可以说服我作基督徒吗！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 亚基帕对保罗说："你想用这样短短的时间就可以说服我作基督徒吗！"
verses.textZhCuv: 亚基帕对保罗说：「你想少微一劝，便叫我作基督徒啊 ！」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian?"
verses.textEnEsv: And Agrippa said to Paul, "In a short time would you persuade me to be a Christian?"
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You almost persuade me to become a Christian."
verses.textEnNlt: Agrippa interrupted him. "Do you think you can persuade me to become a Christian so quickly?"
verses.textEnNasb: Agrippa replied to Paul, " In a short time you are going to persuade me to make a Christian of myself."
verses.textEn: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian?"

verses.textZh: 保罗说："无论时间短也好，时间长也好，我向神所求的，不单是你，而且是今天所有的听众，都能像我一样作基督徒，只是不要有这些锁炼。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗说："无论时间短也好，时间长也好，我向神所求的，不单是你，而且是今天所有的听众，都能像我一样作基督徒，只是不要有这些锁炼。"
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗说：「无论是少劝是多劝，我向神所求的，不但你一个人，就是今天一切听我的，都要像我一样，只是不要像我有这些锁链。」
verses.textEnNiv: Paul replied, "Short time or long—I pray to God that not only you but all who are listening to me today may become what I am, except for these chains."
verses.textEnEsv: And Paul said, "Whether short or long, I would to God that not only you but also all who hear me this day might become such as I am—except for these chains."
verses.textEnNkjv: And Paul said, "I would to God that not only you, but also all who hear me today, might become both almost and altogether such as I am, except for these chains."
verses.textEnNlt: Paul replied, "Whether quickly or not, I pray to God that both you and everyone here in this audience might become the same as I am, except for these chains."
verses.textEnNasb: And Paul said, "I would wish to God that even in a short or long time not only you, but also all who hear me this day would become such as I myself am, except for these chains."
verses.textEn: Paul replied, "Short time or long—I pray to God that not only you but all who are listening to me today may become what I am, except for these chains."

verses.textZh: 亚基帕王、总督和百尼基，还有在座的人都站起来，
verses.textZhCnvs: 亚基帕王、总督和百尼基，还有在座的人都站起来，
verses.textZhCuv: 于是，王和巡抚并百妮基与同坐的人都起来，
verses.textEnNiv: The king rose, and with him the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them.
verses.textEnEsv: Then the king rose, and the governor and Bernice and those who were sitting with them.
verses.textEnNkjv: When he had said these things, the king stood up, as well as the governor and Bernice and those who sat with them;
verses.textEnNlt: Then the king, the governor, Bernice, and all the others stood and left.
verses.textEnNasb: The king stood up and the governor and Bernice, and those who were sitting with them,
verses.textEn: The king rose, and with him the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them.

verses.textZh: 退到一边，彼此谈论，说："这个人并没有犯过甚么该死该绑的罪。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 退到一边，彼此谈论，说："这个人并没有犯过甚么该死该绑的罪。"
verses.textZhCuv: 退到里面，彼此谈论说：「这人并没有犯什么该死该绑的罪。」
verses.textEnNiv: After they left the room, they began saying to one another, "This man is not doing anything that deserves death or imprisonment."
verses.textEnEsv: And when they had withdrawn, they said to one another, "This man is doing nothing to deserve death or imprisonment."
verses.textEnNkjv: and when they had gone aside, they talked among themselves, saying, "This man is doing nothing deserving of death or chains."
verses.textEnNlt: As they went out, they talked it over and agreed, "This man hasn’t done anything to deserve death or imprisonment."
verses.textEnNasb: and when they had gone out, they began talking to one another, saying, "This man is not doing anything deserving death or imprisonment."
verses.textEn: After they left the room, they began saying to one another, "This man is not doing anything that deserves death or imprisonment."

verses.textZh: 亚基帕对非斯都说："这个人若没有向凯撒上诉，早就可以释放了。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 亚基帕对非斯都说："这个人若没有向凯撒上诉，早就可以释放了。"
verses.textZhCuv: 亚基帕又对非斯都说：「这人若没有上告于凯撒，就可以释放了。」
verses.textEnNiv: Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
verses.textEnEsv: And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
verses.textEnNlt: And Agrippa said to Festus, "He could have been set free if he hadn’t appealed to Caesar."
verses.textEnNasb: And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
verses.textEn: Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."

verses.textZh: 他们决定要我们坐船往意大利去，就把保罗和别的囚犯，交给皇家军营里的一个百夫长，名叫犹流。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们决定要我们坐船往意大利去，就把保罗和别的囚犯，交给皇家军营里的一个百夫长，名叫犹流。
verses.textZhCuv: 非斯都既然定规了，叫我们坐船往意大利去，便将保罗和别的囚犯交给御营里的一个百夫长，名叫犹流。
verses.textEnNiv: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
verses.textEnEsv: And when it was decided that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion of the Augustan Cohort named Julius.
verses.textEnNkjv: And when it was decided that we should sail to Italy, they delivered Paul and some other prisoners to one named Julius, a centurion of the Augustan Regiment.
verses.textEnNlt: When the time came, we set sail for Italy. Paul and several other prisoners were placed in the custody of a Roman officer named Julius, a captain of the Imperial Regiment.
verses.textEnNasb: Now when it was decided that we would sail for Italy, they proceeded to turn Paul and some other prisoners over to a centurion of the Augustan cohort, named Julius.
verses.textEn: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.

verses.textZh: 有一艘亚大米田来的船，要开往亚西亚沿岸一带的地方，我们上去，船就开了。跟我们在一起的，还有马其顿的帖撒罗尼迦人亚里达古。
verses.textZhCnvs: 有一艘亚大米田来的船，要开往亚西亚沿岸一带的地方，我们上去，船就开了。跟我们在一起的，还有马其顿的帖撒罗尼迦人亚里达古。
verses.textZhCuv: 有一只亚大米田的船，要沿着亚细亚一带地方的海边走，我们就上了那船开行；有马其顿的帖撒罗尼迦人亚里达古和我们同去。
verses.textEnNiv: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium about to sail for ports along the coast of the province of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
verses.textEnEsv: And embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to the ports along the coast of Asia, we put to sea, accompanied by Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica.
verses.textEnNkjv: So, entering a ship of Adramyttium, we put to sea, meaning to sail along the coasts of Asia. Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, was with us.
verses.textEnNlt: Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was also with us. We left on a ship whose home port was Adramyttium on the northwest coast of the province of Asia; it was scheduled to make several stops at ports along the coast of the province.
verses.textEnNasb: And we boarded an Adramyttian ship that was about to sail to the regions along the coast of Asia, and put out to sea accompanied by Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica.
verses.textEn: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium about to sail for ports along the coast of the province of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

verses.textZh: 第二天到了西顿，犹流宽待保罗，准他去看看朋友，接受他们的招待。
verses.textZhCnvs: 第二天到了西顿，犹流宽待保罗，准他去看看朋友，接受他们的招待。
verses.textZhCuv: 第二天，到了西顿；犹流宽待保罗，准他往朋友那里去，受他们的照应。
verses.textEnNiv: The next day we landed at Sidon; and Julius, in kindness to Paul, allowed him to go to his friends so they might provide for his needs.
verses.textEnEsv: The next day we put in at Sidon. And Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him leave to go to his friends and be cared for.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the next day we landed at Sidon. And Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him liberty to go to his friends and receive care.
verses.textEnNlt: The next day when we docked at Sidon, Julius was very kind to Paul and let him go ashore to visit with friends so they could provide for his needs.
verses.textEnNasb: The next day we put in at Sidon; and Julius treated Paul with consideration and allowed him to go to his friends and receive care.
verses.textEn: The next day we landed at Sidon; and Julius, in kindness to Paul, allowed him to go to his friends so they might provide for his needs.

verses.textZh: 我们又从那里开船，因为逆风，就沿着塞浦路斯背风而行。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们又从那里开船，因为逆风，就沿着塞浦路斯背风而行。
verses.textZhCuv: 从那里又开船，因为风不顺，就贴着塞浦路斯背风岸行去。
verses.textEnNiv: From there we put out to sea again and passed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
verses.textEnEsv: And putting out to sea from there we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were against us.
verses.textEnNkjv: When we had put to sea from there, we sailed under theshelterof Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.textEnNlt: Putting out to sea from there, we encountered strong headwinds that made it difficult to keep the ship on course, so we sailed north of Cyprus between the island and the mainland.
verses.textEnNasb: From there we put out to sea and sailed under the shelter of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.textEn: From there we put out to sea again and passed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.

verses.textZh: 渡过基利家和旁非利亚一带的海面，就到了吕家的每拉。
verses.textZhCnvs: 渡过基利家和旁非利亚一带的海面，就到了吕家的每拉。
verses.textZhCuv: 过了基利家、旁非利亚前面的海，就到了吕家的每拉。
verses.textEnNiv: When we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.
verses.textEnEsv: And when we had sailed across the open sea along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
verses.textEnNkjv: And when we had sailed over the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, acity of Lycia.
verses.textEnNlt: Keeping to the open sea, we passed along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, landing at Myra, in the province of Lycia.
