verses.textEnNasb: When we had sailed through the sea along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.
verses.textEn: When we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.

verses.textZh: 百夫长在那里找到一艘亚历山太来的船，要开往意大利去，就叫我们上了那船。
verses.textZhCnvs: 百夫长在那里找到一艘亚历山太来的船，要开往意大利去，就叫我们上了那船。
verses.textZhCuv: 在那里，百夫长遇见一只亚历山大的船，要往意大利去，便叫我们上了那船。
verses.textEnNiv: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
verses.textEnEsv: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy and put us on board.
verses.textEnNkjv: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy, and he put us on board.
verses.textEnNlt: There the commanding officer found an Egyptian ship from Alexandria that was bound for Italy, and he put us on board.
verses.textEnNasb: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy, and he put us aboard it.
verses.textEn: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.

verses.textZh: 一连几天，船都走得很慢，好不容易才到了革尼土的对面。因为有风阻挡着我们，就沿着克里特背风而行，从撒摩尼对面经过，
verses.textZhCnvs: 一连几天，船都走得很慢，好不容易才到了革尼土的对面。因为有风阻挡着我们，就沿着克里特背风而行，从撒摩尼对面经过，
verses.textZhCuv: 一连多日，船行得慢，仅仅来到革尼土的对面。因为被风拦阻，就贴着克里特背风岸，从撒摩尼对面行过。
verses.textEnNiv: We made slow headway for many days and had difficulty arriving off Cnidus. When the wind did not allow us to hold our course, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
verses.textEnEsv: We sailed slowly for a number of days and arrived with difficulty off Cnidus, and as the wind did not allow us to go farther, we sailed under the lee of Crete off Salmone.
verses.textEnNkjv: When we had sailed slowly many days, and arrived with difficulty off Cnidus, the wind not permitting us to proceed, we sailed under theshelterof Crete off Salmone.
verses.textEnNlt: We had several days of slow sailing, and after great difficulty we finally neared Cnidus. But the wind was against us, so we sailed across to Crete and along the sheltered coast of the island, past the cape of Salmone.
verses.textEnNasb: When we had sailed slowly for a good many days, and with difficulty had arrived off Cnidus, since the wind did not permit us to go farther, we sailed under the shelter of Crete, off Salmone;
verses.textEn: We made slow headway for many days and had difficulty arriving off Cnidus. When the wind did not allow us to hold our course, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

verses.textZh: 沿着海岸行驶，航程很艰难，后来才到了靠近拉西亚城一个名叫美港的地方。
verses.textZhCnvs: 沿着海岸行驶，航程很艰难，后来才到了靠近拉西亚城一个名叫美港的地方。
verses.textZhCuv: 我们沿岸行走，仅仅来到一个地方，名叫佳澳；离那里不远，有拉西亚城。
verses.textEnNiv: We moved along the coast with difficulty and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
verses.textEnEsv: Coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.
verses.textEnNkjv: Passing it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
verses.textEnNlt: We struggled along the coast with great difficulty and finally arrived at Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
verses.textEnNasb: and with difficulty sailing past it, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.
verses.textEn: We moved along the coast with difficulty and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

verses.textZh: 过了相当的时候，连禁食节也过去了，所以航行很危险，保罗就劝告他们，
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了相当的时候，连禁食节也过去了，所以航行很危险，保罗就劝告他们，
verses.textZhCuv: 走的日子多了，已经过了禁食的节期，行船又危险，保罗就劝众人说：
verses.textEnNiv: Much time had been lost, and sailing had already become dangerous because by now it was after the Day of Atonement. So Paul warned them,
verses.textEnEsv: Since much time had passed, and the voyage was now dangerous because even the Fast was already over, Paul advised them,
verses.textEnNkjv: Now when much time had been spent, and sailing was now dangerous because the Fast was already over, Paul advised them,
verses.textEnNlt: We had lost a lot of time. The weather was becoming dangerous for sea travel because it was so late in the fall, and Paul spoke to the ship’s officers about it.
verses.textEnNasb: When considerable time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, since even the fast was already over, Paul started admonishing them,
verses.textEn: Much time had been lost, and sailing had already become dangerous because by now it was after the Day of Atonement. So Paul warned them,

verses.textZh: 说："各位，我看这次航行，不单货物和船只要遭到损失，大受破坏，连我们的性命也难保。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 说："各位，我看这次航行，不单货物和船只要遭到损失，大受破坏，连我们的性命也难保。"
verses.textZhCuv: 「众位，我看这次行船，不但货物和船要受损伤，大遭破坏，连我们的性命也难保。」
verses.textEnNiv: "Men, I can see that our voyage is going to be disastrous and bring great loss to ship and cargo, and to our own lives also."
verses.textEnEsv: saying, "Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives."
verses.textEnNkjv: saying, "Men, I perceive that this voyage will end with disaster and much loss, not only of the cargo and ship, but also our lives."
verses.textEnNlt: "Men," he said, "I believe there is trouble ahead if we go on—shipwreck, loss of cargo, and danger to our lives as well."
verses.textEnNasb: saying to them, "Men, I perceive that the voyage will certainly be with damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives."
verses.textEn: "Men, I can see that our voyage is going to be disastrous and bring great loss to ship and cargo, and to our own lives also."

verses.textZh: 但百夫长宁愿相信船长和船主的话，却不相信保罗所说的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 但百夫长宁愿相信船长和船主的话，却不相信保罗所说的。
verses.textZhCuv: 但百夫长信从掌船的和船主，不信从保罗所说的。
verses.textEnNiv: But the centurion, instead of listening to what Paul said, followed the advice of the pilot and of the owner of the ship.
verses.textEnEsv: But the centurion paid more attention to the pilot and to the owner of the ship than to what Paul said.
verses.textEnNkjv: Nevertheless the centurion was more persuaded by the helmsman and the owner of the ship than by the things spoken by Paul.
verses.textEnNlt: But the officer in charge of the prisoners listened more to the ship’s captain and the owner than to Paul.
verses.textEnNasb: But the centurion was more persuaded by the pilot and the captain of the ship than by what was being said by Paul.
verses.textEn: But the centurion, instead of listening to what Paul said, followed the advice of the pilot and of the owner of the ship.

verses.textZh: 而且这港口不适宜过冬，所以大多数人主张离开那里，也许可以到非尼基去过冬。非尼基是克里特的一个港口，一面向西南，一面向西北。
verses.textZhCnvs: 而且这港口不适宜过冬，所以大多数人主张离开那里，也许可以到非尼基去过冬。非尼基是克里特的一个港口，一面向西南，一面向西北。
verses.textZhCuv: 且因在这海口过冬不便，船上的人就多半说，不如开船离开这地方，或者能到菲尼基过冬。菲尼基是克里特的一个海口，一面朝东北，一面朝东南。
verses.textEnNiv: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided that we should sail on, hoping to reach Phoenix and winter there. This was a harbor in Crete, facing both southwest and northwest.
verses.textEnEsv: And because the harbor was not suitable to spend the winter in, the majority decided to put out to sea from there, on the chance that somehow they could reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete, facing both southwest and northwest, and spend the winter there.
verses.textEnNkjv: And because the harbor was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised to set sail from there also, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete opening toward the southwest and northwest, and winter there.
verses.textEnNlt: And since Fair Havens was an exposed harbor—a poor place to spend the winter—most of the crew wanted to go on to Phoenix, farther up the coast of Crete, and spend the winter there. Phoenix was a good harbor with only a southwest and northwest exposure.
verses.textEnNasb: The harbor was not suitable for wintering, so the majority reached a decision to put out to sea from there, if somehow they could reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete facing southwest and northwest, and spend the winter there.
verses.textEn: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided that we should sail on, hoping to reach Phoenix and winter there. This was a harbor in Crete, facing both southwest and northwest.

verses.textZh: 这时南风徐徐地吹来，他们以为风势有利，就起锚沿着克里特航行。
verses.textZhCnvs: 这时南风徐徐地吹来，他们以为风势有利，就起锚沿着克里特航行。
verses.textZhCuv: 这时，微微起了南风，他们以为得意，就起了锚，贴近克里特行去。
verses.textEnNiv: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they saw their opportunity; so they weighed anchor and sailed along the shore of Crete.
verses.textEnEsv: Now when the south wind blew gently, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to the shore.
verses.textEnNkjv: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their desire, putting out to sea, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.textEnNlt: When a light wind began blowing from the south, the sailors thought they could make it. So they pulled up anchor and sailed close to the shore of Crete.
verses.textEnNasb: When a moderate south wind came up, thinking that they had attained their purpose, they weighed anchor and began sailing along Crete, closer to shore.
verses.textEn: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they saw their opportunity; so they weighed anchor and sailed along the shore of Crete.

verses.textZh: 可是过了不久，有一股名叫"友拉革罗" 的飓风，向岛上吹袭。
verses.textZhCnvs: 可是过了不久，有一股名叫"友拉革罗" 的飓风，向岛上吹袭。
verses.textZhCuv: 不多几时，狂风从岛上扑下来；那风名叫「友拉革罗」。
verses.textEnNiv: Before very long, a wind of hurricane force, called the Northeaster, swept down from the island.
verses.textEnEsv: But soon a tempestuous wind, called the northeaster, struck down from the land.
verses.textEnNkjv: But not long after, a tempestuous head wind arose, called Euroclydon.
verses.textEnNlt: But the weather changed abruptly, and a wind of typhoon strength (called a "northeaster") burst across the island and blew us out to sea.
verses.textEnNasb: But before very long a violent wind, called Euraquilo, rushed down from the land;
verses.textEn: Before very long, a wind of hurricane force, called the Northeaster, swept down from the island.

verses.textZh: 船给风困住了，不能迎风前行，只好随着风向飘流。
verses.textZhCnvs: 船给风困住了，不能迎风前行，只好随着风向飘流。
verses.textZhCuv: 船被风抓住，敌不住风，我们就任风刮去。
verses.textEnNiv: The ship was caught by the storm and could not head into the wind; so we gave way to it and were driven along.
verses.textEnEsv: And when the ship was caught and could not face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.
verses.textEnNkjv: So when the ship was caught, and could not head into the wind, we let her drive.
verses.textEnNlt: The sailors couldn’t turn the ship into the wind, so they gave up and let it run before the gale.
verses.textEnNasb: and when the ship was caught in it and could not head up into the wind, we gave up and let ourselves be driven by the wind.
verses.textEn: The ship was caught by the storm and could not head into the wind; so we gave way to it and were driven along.

verses.textZh: 有一个小岛名叫高达，我们就在这岛的背风岸急航，好不容易才把救生艇拉住。
verses.textZhCnvs: 有一个小岛名叫高达，我们就在这岛的背风岸急航，好不容易才把救生艇拉住。
verses.textZhCuv: 贴着一个小岛的背风岸奔行，那岛名叫高大，在那里仅仅收住了小船。
verses.textEnNiv: As we passed to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were hardly able to make the lifeboat secure,
verses.textEnEsv: Running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, we managed with difficulty to secure the ship’s boat.
verses.textEnNkjv: And running under theshelterof an island called Clauda, we secured the skiff with difficulty.
verses.textEnNlt: We sailed along the sheltered side of a small island named Cauda, where with great difficulty we hoisted aboard the lifeboat being towed behind us.
verses.textEnNasb: Running under the shelter of a small island called Cauda, we were able to get the ship’s boat under control only with difficulty.
verses.textEn: As we passed to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were hardly able to make the lifeboat secure,

verses.textZh: 水手把艇拉上来，用缆索绕过船身捆好。他们怕船在赛耳底搁浅，就收下船帆，任船飘流。
verses.textZhCnvs: 水手把艇拉上来，用缆索绕过船身捆好。他们怕船在赛耳底搁浅，就收下船帆，任船飘流。
verses.textZhCuv: 既然把小船拉上来，就用缆索捆绑船底，又恐怕在赛耳底沙滩上搁了浅，就落下篷来，任船飘去。
verses.textEnNiv: so the men hoisted it aboard. Then they passed ropes under the ship itself to hold it together. Because they were afraid they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship be driven along.
verses.textEnEsv: After hoisting it up, they used supports to undergird the ship. Then, fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis, they lowered the gear, and thus they were driven along.
verses.textEnNkjv: When they had taken it on board, they used cables to undergird the ship; and fearing lest they should run aground on the Syrtis Sands, they struck sail and so were driven.
verses.textEnNlt: Then the sailors bound ropes around the hull of the ship to strengthen it. They were afraid of being driven across to the sandbars of Syrtis off the African coast, so they lowered the sea anchor to slow the ship and were driven before the wind.
verses.textEnNasb: After they had hoisted it up, they used supporting cables in undergirding the ship; and fearing that they might run aground on the shallows of Syrtis, they let down the sea anchor and let themselves be driven along in this way.
verses.textEn: so the men hoisted it aboard. Then they passed ropes under the ship itself to hold it together. Because they were afraid they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship be driven along.

verses.textZh: 风浪把我们颠簸得很厉害，第二天他们就把货物拋在海里，
verses.textZhCnvs: 风浪把我们颠簸得很厉害，第二天他们就把货物拋在海里，
verses.textZhCuv: 我们被风浪逼得甚急，第二天众人就把货物抛在海里。
verses.textEnNiv: We took such a violent battering from the storm that the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard.
verses.textEnEsv: Since we were violently storm-tossed, they began the next day to jettison the cargo.
verses.textEnNkjv: And because we were exceedingly tempest-tossed, the next day they lightened the ship.
verses.textEnNlt: The next day, as gale-force winds continued to batter the ship, the crew began throwing the cargo overboard.
verses.textEnNasb: The next day as we were being violently tossed by the storm, they began to jettison the cargo;
verses.textEn: We took such a violent battering from the storm that the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard.

verses.textZh: 第三天又亲手把船上的用具扔掉。
verses.textZhCnvs: 第三天又亲手把船上的用具扔掉。
verses.textZhCuv: 到第三天，他们又亲手把船上的器具抛弃了。
verses.textEnNiv: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
verses.textEnEsv: And on the third day they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
verses.textEnNkjv: On the third day we threw the ship’s tackle overboard with our own hands.
verses.textEnNlt: The following day they even took some of the ship’s gear and threw it overboard.
verses.textEnNasb: and on the third day they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
verses.textEn: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

verses.textZh: 好几天，都看不见星星和太阳，狂风大浪催逼着我们，这样看来，我们连生还的希望都没有了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 好几天，都看不见星星和太阳，狂风大浪催逼着我们，这样看来，我们连生还的希望都没有了。
verses.textZhCuv: 太阳和星辰多日不显露，又有狂风大浪催逼，我们得救的指望就都绝了。
verses.textEnNiv: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the storm continued raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
verses.textEnEsv: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope of our being saved was at last abandoned.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now when neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small tempest beat on us, all hope that we would be saved was finally given up.
verses.textEnNlt: The terrible storm raged for many days, blotting out the sun and the stars, until at last all hope was gone.
verses.textEnNasb: Since neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small storm was assailing us, from then on all hope of our being saved was slowly abandoned.
verses.textEn: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the storm continued raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.

verses.textZh: 大家很久没有吃饭了，保罗就站在他们中间，说："各位，你们本来应该听我的话不离开克里特，就不会遭受这场损失和破坏了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大家很久没有吃饭了，保罗就站在他们中间，说："各位，你们本来应该听我的话不离开克里特，就不会遭受这场损失和破坏了。
verses.textZhCuv: 众人多日没有吃什么，保罗就出来站在他们中间，说：「众位，你们本该听我的话，不离开克里特，免得遭这样的伤损破坏。
verses.textEnNiv: After they had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up before them and said: "Men, you should have taken my advice not to sail from Crete; then you would have spared yourselves this damage and loss.
verses.textEnEsv: Since they had been without food for a long time, Paul stood up among them and said, "Men, you should have listened to me and not have set sail from Crete and incurred this injury and loss.
verses.textEnNkjv: But after long abstinence from food, then Paul stood in the midst of them and said, "Men, you should have listened to me, and not have sailed from Crete and incurred this disaster and loss.
verses.textEnNlt: No one had eaten for a long time. Finally, Paul called the crew together and said, "Men, you should have listened to me in the first place and not left Crete. You would have avoided all this damage and loss.
verses.textEnNasb: When many had lost their appetites, Paul then stood among them and said, " Men, you should have followed my advice and not have set sail from Crete, and thereby spared yourselves this damage and loss.
verses.textEn: After they had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up before them and said: "Men, you should have taken my advice not to sail from Crete; then you would have spared yourselves this damage and loss.

verses.textZh: 现在我劝你们放心。除了这艘船以外，你们没有一个人会丧命的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 现在我劝你们放心。除了这艘船以外，你们没有一个人会丧命的。
verses.textZhCuv: 现在我还劝你们放心，你们的性命一个也不失丧，惟独失丧这船。
verses.textEnNiv: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed.
verses.textEnEsv: Yet now I urge you to take heart, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
verses.textEnNkjv: And now I urge you to take heart, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
verses.textEnNlt: But take courage! None of you will lose your lives, even though the ship will go down.
verses.textEnNasb: And yet now I urge you to keep up your courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
verses.textEn: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed.

verses.textZh: 因为我所归属所事奉的神，他的使者昨天夜里站在我的旁边，说：
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为我所归属所事奉的神，他的使者昨天夜里站在我的旁边，说：
verses.textZhCuv: 因我所属所事奉的神，他的使者昨夜站在我旁边，说：
verses.textEnNiv: Last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me
verses.textEnEsv: For this very night there stood before me an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I worship,
verses.textEnNkjv: For there stood by me this night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve,
verses.textEnNlt: For last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me,
verses.textEnNasb: For this very night an angel of the God to whom I belong, whom I also serve, came to me,
verses.textEn: Last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me

verses.textZh: ‘保罗，不要怕。你必定可以站在凯撒面前；神已经把那些和你同船的人赐给你了。’
verses.textZhCnvs: ‘保罗，不要怕。你必定可以站在凯撒面前；神已经把那些和你同船的人赐给你了。’
verses.textZhCuv: 『保罗，不要害怕，你必定站在凯撒面前，并且与你同船的人，神都赐给你了。』
verses.textEnNiv: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar; and God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.’
verses.textEnEsv: and he said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
verses.textEnNkjv: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must be brought before Caesar; and indeed God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
verses.textEnNlt: and he said, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul, for you will surely stand trial before Caesar! What’s more, God in his goodness has granted safety to everyone sailing with you.’
verses.textEnNasb: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar; and behold, God has graciously granted you all those who are sailing with you.’
verses.textEn: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar; and God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.’

verses.textZh: 所以，各位请放心。我相信神对我怎样说，也必怎样成就。
verses.textZhCnvs: 所以，各位请放心。我相信神对我怎样说，也必怎样成就。
verses.textZhCuv: 所以众位可以放心，我信神他怎样对我说，事情也要怎样成就。
verses.textEnNiv: So keep up your courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as he told me.
verses.textEnEsv: So take heart, men, for I have faith in God that it will be exactly as I have been told.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be just as it was told me.
verses.textEnNlt: So take courage! For I believe God. It will be just as he said.
verses.textEnNasb: Therefore, keep up your courage, men, for I believe God that it will turn out exactly as I have been told.
verses.textEn: So keep up your courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as he told me.

verses.textZh: 不过我们必会搁浅在一个海岛上。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 不过我们必会搁浅在一个海岛上。"
verses.textZhCuv: 只是我们必要撞在一个岛上。」
verses.textEnNiv: Nevertheless, we must run aground on some island."
verses.textEnEsv: But we must run aground on some island."
verses.textEnNkjv: However, we must run aground on a certain island."
verses.textEnNlt: But we will be shipwrecked on an island."
verses.textEnNasb: But we must run aground on a certain island."
verses.textEn: Nevertheless, we must run aground on some island."

verses.textZh: 到了第十四天的晚上，我们在亚得里亚海飘来飘去。约在半夜的时候，水手以为接近了陆地，
verses.textZhCnvs: 到了第十四天的晚上，我们在亚得里亚海飘来飘去。约在半夜的时候，水手以为接近了陆地，
verses.textZhCuv: 到了第十四天夜间，船在亚得里亚海飘来飘去。约到半夜，水手以为渐近旱地，
verses.textEnNiv: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea, when about midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
verses.textEnEsv: When the fourteenth night had come, as we were being driven across the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors suspected that they were nearing land.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven up and down in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors sensed that they were drawing near some land.
verses.textEnNlt: About midnight on the fourteenth night of the storm, as we were being driven across the Sea of Adria, the sailors sensed land was near.
verses.textEnNasb: But when the fourteenth night came, as we were being driven about in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors began to suspect that they were approaching some land.
verses.textEn: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea, when about midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.

verses.textZh: 就探测一下，深三十六公尺；稍往前行，再探测一下，深二十七公尺。
verses.textZhCnvs: 就探测一下，深三十六公尺；稍往前行，再探测一下，深二十七公尺。
verses.textZhCuv: 就探深浅，探得有十二丈；稍往前行，又探深浅，探得有九丈。
verses.textEnNiv: They took soundings and found that the water was a hundred and twenty feet deep. A short time later they took soundings again and found it was ninety feet deep.
verses.textEnEsv: So they took a sounding and found twenty fathoms. A little farther on they took a sounding again and found fifteen fathoms.
verses.textEnNkjv: And they took soundings and found it to be twenty fathoms; and when they had gone a little farther, they took soundings again and found it to be fifteen fathoms.
verses.textEnNlt: They dropped a weighted line and found that the water was 120 feet deep. But a little later they measured again and found it was only 90 feet deep.
verses.textEnNasb: And they took soundings and found it to be twenty fathoms; and a little farther on they took another sounding and found it to be fifteen fathoms.
verses.textEn: They took soundings and found that the water was a hundred and twenty feet deep. A short time later they took soundings again and found it was ninety feet deep.

verses.textZh: 他们怕我们会在乱石上搁浅，就从船尾拋下四个锚，期待着天亮。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们怕我们会在乱石上搁浅，就从船尾拋下四个锚，期待着天亮。
verses.textZhCuv: 恐怕撞在石头上，就从船尾抛下四个锚，盼望天亮。
verses.textEnNiv: Fearing that we would be dashed against the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.
verses.textEnEsv: And fearing that we might run on the rocks, they let down four anchors from the stern and prayed for day to come.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then, fearing lest we should run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern, and prayed for day to come.
verses.textEnNlt: At this rate they were afraid we would soon be driven against the rocks along the shore, so they threw out four anchors from the back of the ship and prayed for daylight.
verses.textEnNasb: Fearing that we might run aground somewhere on the rocks, they cast four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
verses.textEn: Fearing that we would be dashed against the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.

verses.textZh: 水手们想要离船逃走，就把救生艇放在海上，假装要从船头拋锚的样子。
verses.textZhCnvs: 水手们想要离船逃走，就把救生艇放在海上，假装要从船头拋锚的样子。
verses.textZhCuv: 水手想要逃出船去，把小船放在海里，假作要从船头抛锚的样子。
verses.textEnNiv: In an attempt to escape from the ship, the sailors let the lifeboat down into the sea, pretending they were going to lower some anchors from the bow.
verses.textEnEsv: And as the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship, and had lowered the ship’s boat into the sea under pretense of laying out anchors from the bow,
verses.textEnNkjv: And as the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship, when they had let down the skiff into the sea, under pretense of putting out anchors from the prow,
verses.textEnNlt: Then the sailors tried to abandon the ship; they lowered the lifeboat as though they were going to put out anchors from the front of the ship.
verses.textEnNasb: But as the sailors were trying to escape from the ship and had let down the ship’s boat into the sea, on the pretense that they were going to lay out anchors from the bow,
verses.textEn: In an attempt to escape from the ship, the sailors let the lifeboat down into the sea, pretending they were going to lower some anchors from the bow.

verses.textZh: 保罗对百夫长和士兵说："这些人若不留在船上，你们就性命难保！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗对百夫长和士兵说："这些人若不留在船上，你们就性命难保！"
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗对百夫长和兵丁说：「这些人若不等在船上，你们必不能得救。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved."
verses.textEnEsv: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved."
verses.textEnNkjv: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved."
verses.textEnNlt: But Paul said to the commanding officer and the soldiers, "You will all die unless the sailors stay aboard."
verses.textEnNasb: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men remain on the ship, you yourselves cannot be saved."
verses.textEn: Then Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved."

verses.textZh: 于是士兵砍断救生艇的绳子，任它掉下去。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是士兵砍断救生艇的绳子，任它掉下去。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是兵丁砍断小船的绳子，由它飘去。
verses.textEnNiv: So the soldiers cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it drift away.
verses.textEnEsv: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the ship’s boat and let it go.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the skiff and let it fall off.
verses.textEnNlt: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and let it drift away.
verses.textEnNasb: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the ship’s boat and let it fall away.
verses.textEn: So the soldiers cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it drift away.

verses.textZh: 天快亮的时候，保罗劝大家吃饭，说："你们一直不吃东西，挨饿苦候，到今天已经十四天了！
verses.textZhCnvs: 天快亮的时候，保罗劝大家吃饭，说："你们一直不吃东西，挨饿苦候，到今天已经十四天了！
verses.textZhCuv: 天渐亮的时候，保罗劝众人都吃饭，说：「你们悬望忍饿不吃什么，已经十四天了。
verses.textEnNiv: Just before dawn Paul urged them all to eat. "For the last fourteen days," he said, "you have been in constant suspense and have gone without food—you haven’t eaten anything.
verses.textEnEsv: As day was about to dawn, Paul urged them all to take some food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day that you have continued in suspense and without food, having taken nothing.
verses.textEnNkjv: And as day was about to dawn, Paul implored them all to take food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day you have waited and continued without food, and eaten nothing.
verses.textEnNlt: Just as day was dawning, Paul urged everyone to eat. "You have been so worried that you haven’t touched food for two weeks," he said.
verses.textEnNasb: Until the day was about to dawn, Paul kept encouraging them all to take some food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day that you have been constantly watching and going without eating, having taken in nothing.
verses.textEn: Just before dawn Paul urged them all to eat. "For the last fourteen days," he said, "you have been in constant suspense and have gone without food—you haven’t eaten anything.

verses.textZh: 所以，我劝你们吃点饭，这可以维持你们的性命！因为你们没有人会失掉一根头发。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 所以，我劝你们吃点饭，这可以维持你们的性命！因为你们没有人会失掉一根头发。"
verses.textZhCuv: 所以我劝你们吃饭，这是关乎你们救命的事；因为你们各人连一根头发也不至于损坏。」
verses.textEnNiv: Now I urge you to take some food. You need it to survive. Not one of you will lose a single hair from his head."
verses.textEnEsv: Therefore I urge you to take some food. For it will give you strength, for not a hair is to perish from the head of any of you."
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore I urge you to take nourishment, for this is for your survival, since not a hair will fall from the head of any of you."
verses.textEnNlt: "Please eat something now for your own good. For not a hair of your heads will perish."
verses.textEnNasb: Therefore, I encourage you to take some food, for this is for your survival, for not a hair from the head of any of you will perish."
verses.textEn: Now I urge you to take some food. You need it to survive. Not one of you will lose a single hair from his head."

verses.textZh: 保罗说了这话，就拿起饼来，在众人面前感谢神，然后擘开来吃。
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗说了这话，就拿起饼来，在众人面前感谢神，然后擘开来吃。
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗说了这话，就拿着饼，在众人面前祝谢了神，擘开吃。
verses.textEnNiv: After he said this, he took some bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
verses.textEnEsv: And when he had said these things, he took bread, and giving thanks to God in the presence of all he broke it and began to eat.
verses.textEnNkjv: And when he had said these things, he took bread and gave thanks to God in the presence of them all; and when he had broken it he began to eat.
verses.textEnNlt: Then he took some bread, gave thanks to God before them all, and broke off a piece and ate it.
verses.textEnNasb: Having said this, he took bread and gave thanks to God in the presence of them all, and he broke it and began to eat.
verses.textEn: After he said this, he took some bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.

verses.textZh: 于是大家都安心吃饭了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是大家都安心吃饭了。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是他们都放下心，也就吃了。
verses.textEnNiv: They were all encouraged and ate some food themselves.
verses.textEnEsv: Then they all were encouraged and ate some food themselves.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then they were all encouraged, and also took food themselves.
verses.textEnNlt: Then everyone was encouraged and began to eat—
verses.textEnNasb: All of them were encouraged and they themselves also took food.
verses.textEn: They were all encouraged and ate some food themselves.

verses.textZh: 我们在船上的共有二百七十六人，
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们在船上的共有二百七十六人，
verses.textZhCuv: 我们在船上的共有二百七十六个人。
verses.textEnNiv: Altogether there were 276 of us on board.
verses.textEnEsv: (We were in all 276 persons in the ship.)
verses.textEnNkjv: And in all we were two hundred and seventy-six persons on the ship.
verses.textEnNlt: all 276 of us who were on board.
verses.textEnNasb: We were 276 people on the ship in all.
verses.textEn: Altogether there were 276 of us on board.

verses.textZh: 大家吃饱了，把麦子拋在海里，好减轻船的负荷。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大家吃饱了，把麦子拋在海里，好减轻船的负荷。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们吃饱了，就把船上的麦子抛在海里，为要叫船轻一点。
verses.textEnNiv: When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
verses.textEnEsv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
verses.textEnNkjv: So when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship and threw out the wheat into the sea.
verses.textEnNlt: After eating, the crew lightened the ship further by throwing the cargo of wheat overboard.
verses.textEnNasb: When they had eaten enough, they began lightening the ship by throwing the wheat out into the sea.
verses.textEn: When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.

verses.textZh: 天亮的时候，他们不认得那个地方，只看见一个可以登岸的海湾，就有意尽可能把船拢岸。
verses.textZhCnvs: 天亮的时候，他们不认得那个地方，只看见一个可以登岸的海湾，就有意尽可能把船拢岸。
verses.textZhCuv: 到了天亮，他们不认识那地方，但见一个海湾，有岸可登，就商议能把船拢进去不能。
verses.textEnNiv: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they saw a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
verses.textEnEsv: Now when it was day, they did not recognize the land, but they noticed a bay with a beach, on which they planned if possible to run the ship ashore.
verses.textEnNkjv: When it was day, they did not recognize the land; but they observed a bay with a beach, onto which they planned to run the ship if possible.
verses.textEnNlt: When morning dawned, they didn’t recognize the coastline, but they saw a bay with a beach and wondered if they could get to shore by running the ship aground.
verses.textEnNasb: Now when day came, they could not recognize the land; but they did notice a bay with a beach, and they resolved to run the ship onto it if they could.
verses.textEn: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they saw a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.

verses.textZh: 于是把锚砍掉，丢在海里，同时又松开舵绳，拉起前帆，顺风向岸驶去。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是把锚砍掉，丢在海里，同时又松开舵绳，拉起前帆，顺风向岸驶去。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是砍断缆索，弃锚在海里；同时也松开舵绳，拉起头篷，顺着风向岸行去。
verses.textEnNiv: Cutting loose the anchors, they left them in the sea and at the same time untied the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
verses.textEnEsv: So they cast off the anchors and left them in the sea, at the same time loosening the ropes that tied the rudders. Then hoisting the foresail to the wind they made for the beach.
verses.textEnNkjv: And they let go the anchors and left them in the sea, meanwhile loosing the rudder ropes; and they hoisted the mainsail to the wind and made for shore.
verses.textEnNlt: So they cut off the anchors and left them in the sea. Then they lowered the rudders, raised the foresail, and headed toward shore.
verses.textEnNasb: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea while at the same time they were loosening the ropes of the rudders; and they hoisted the foresail to the wind and were heading for the beach.
verses.textEn: Cutting loose the anchors, they left them in the sea and at the same time untied the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.

verses.textZh: 但在海水夹流的地方，船就搁了浅，船头胶着不动，船尾被海浪冲击，就损坏了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 但在海水夹流的地方，船就搁了浅，船头胶着不动，船尾被海浪冲击，就损坏了。
verses.textZhCuv: 但遇着两水夹流的地方，就把船搁了浅；船头胶住不动，船尾被浪的猛力冲坏。
verses.textEnNiv: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was broken to pieces by the pounding of the surf.
verses.textEnEsv: But striking a reef, they ran the vessel aground. The bow stuck and remained immovable, and the stern was being broken up by the surf.
verses.textEnNkjv: But striking a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the prow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was being broken up by the violence of the waves.
verses.textEnNlt: But they hit a shoal and ran the ship aground too soon. The bow of the ship stuck fast, while the stern was repeatedly smashed by the force of the waves and began to break apart.
verses.textEnNasb: But they struck a reef where two seas met and ran the ship aground; and the prow stuck firmly and remained immovable, while the stern started to break up due to the force of the waves.
verses.textEn: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was broken to pieces by the pounding of the surf.

verses.textZh: 士兵想把囚犯都杀掉，免得有人游泳逃脱。
verses.textZhCnvs: 士兵想把囚犯都杀掉，免得有人游泳逃脱。
verses.textZhCuv: 兵丁的意思要把囚犯杀了，恐怕有洑水脱逃的。
verses.textEnNiv: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent any of them from swimming away and escaping.
verses.textEnEsv: The soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any should swim away and escape.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.
verses.textEnNlt: The soldiers wanted to kill the prisoners to make sure they didn’t swim ashore and escape.
verses.textEnNasb: The soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim away and escape;
verses.textEn: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent any of them from swimming away and escaping.

verses.textZh: 但百夫长想要救保罗，就阻止他们这样行。他吩咐会游泳的跳下水去，先到岸上，
verses.textZhCnvs: 但百夫长想要救保罗，就阻止他们这样行。他吩咐会游泳的跳下水去，先到岸上，
verses.textZhCuv: 但百夫长要救保罗，不准他们任意而行，就吩咐会洑水的，跳下水去先上岸；
verses.textEnNiv: But the centurion wanted to spare Paul’s life and kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
verses.textEnEsv: But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and make for the land,
verses.textEnNkjv: But the centurion, wanting to save Paul, kept them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should jump overboard first and get to land,
verses.textEnNlt: But the commanding officer wanted to spare Paul, so he didn’t let them carry out their plan. Then he ordered all who could swim to jump overboard first and make for land.
verses.textEnNasb: but the centurion, wanting to bring Paul safely through, kept them from accomplishing their intention, and commanded that those who could swim were to jump overboard first and get to land,
verses.textEn: But the centurion wanted to spare Paul’s life and kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

verses.textZh: 其余的人可以用木板，或船上的器具上岸。这样，大家都安全地上岸了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 其余的人可以用木板，或船上的器具上岸。这样，大家都安全地上岸了。
verses.textZhCuv: 其余的人可以用板子或船上的零碎东西上岸。这样，众人都得了救，上了岸。
verses.textEnNiv: The rest were to get there on planks or on other pieces of the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.
verses.textEnEsv: and the rest on planks or on pieces of the ship. And so it was that all were brought safely to land.
verses.textEnNkjv: and the rest, some on boards and some on parts of the ship. And so it was that they all escaped safely to land.
verses.textEnNlt: The others held on to planks or debris from the broken ship. So everyone escaped safely to shore.
verses.textEnNasb: and the rest were to follow, some on planks, and others on various things from the ship. And so it happened that they all were brought safely to land.
verses.textEn: The rest were to get there on planks or on other pieces of the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.

verses.textZh: 我们脱险之后，才知道那岛名叫马尔他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们脱险之后，才知道那岛名叫马尔他。
verses.textZhCuv: 我们既已得救，才知道那岛名叫马耳他。
verses.textEnNiv: Once safely on shore, we found out that the island was called Malta.
verses.textEnEsv: After we were brought safely through, we then learned that the island was called Malta.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now when they had escaped, they then found out that the island was called Malta.
verses.textEnNlt: Once we were safe on shore, we learned that we were on the island of Malta.
verses.textEnNasb: When they had been brought safely through, then we found out that the island was called Malta.
verses.textEn: Once safely on shore, we found out that the island was called Malta.

verses.textZh: 当地的人对我们非常友善；因为下过一场雨，天气又冷，他们就生了火来招待我们。
verses.textZhCnvs: 当地的人对我们非常友善；因为下过一场雨，天气又冷，他们就生了火来招待我们。
verses.textZhCuv: 土人看待我们，有非常的情分；因为当时下雨，天气又冷，就生火接待我们众人。
verses.textEnNiv: The islanders showed us unusual kindness. They built a fire and welcomed us all because it was raining and cold.
verses.textEnEsv: The native people showed us unusual kindness, for they kindled a fire and welcomed us all, because it had begun to rain and was cold.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the natives showed us unusual kindness; for they kindled a fire and made us all welcome, because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.
verses.textEnNlt: The people of the island were very kind to us. It was cold and rainy, so they built a fire on the shore to welcome us.
verses.textEnNasb: The natives showed us extraordinary kindness, for they kindled a fire and took us all in because of the rain that had started and because of the cold.
verses.textEn: The islanders showed us unusual kindness. They built a fire and welcomed us all because it was raining and cold.

verses.textZh: 保罗拾了一捆干柴，放在火上的时候，有一条毒蛇，受不住热，爬了出来，缠住他的手。
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗拾了一捆干柴，放在火上的时候，有一条毒蛇，受不住热，爬了出来，缠住他的手。
verses.textZhCuv: 那时，保罗拾起一捆柴，放在火上，有一条毒蛇，因为热了出来，咬住他的手。
verses.textEnNiv: Paul gathered a pile of brushwood and, as he put it on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself on his hand.
verses.textEnEsv: When Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and put them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.
verses.textEnNkjv: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.textEnNlt: As Paul gathered an armful of sticks and was laying them on the fire, a poisonous snake, driven out by the heat, bit him on the hand.
verses.textEnNasb: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened itself on his hand.
verses.textEn: Paul gathered a pile of brushwood and, as he put it on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself on his hand.

verses.textZh: 当地的人看见那条蛇悬在他手上，就彼此说："这个人一定是凶手，虽然从海里脱险，天理也不容他活着！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 当地的人看见那条蛇悬在他手上，就彼此说："这个人一定是凶手，虽然从海里脱险，天理也不容他活着！"
verses.textZhCuv: 土人看见那毒蛇悬在他手上，就彼此说：「这人必是个凶手，虽然从海里救上来，天理还不容他活着。」
verses.textEnNiv: When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, "This man must be a murderer; for though he escaped from the sea, the goddess Justice has not allowed him to live."
verses.textEnEsv: When the native people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer. Though he has escaped from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live."
verses.textEnNkjv: So when the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet justice does not allow to live."
verses.textEnNlt: The people of the island saw it hanging from his hand and said to each other, "A murderer, no doubt! Though he escaped the sea, justice will not permit him to live."
verses.textEnNasb: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they began saying to one another, "Undoubtedly this man is a murderer, and though he has been saved from the sea, justice has not allowed him to live."
verses.textEn: When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, "This man must be a murderer; for though he escaped from the sea, the goddess Justice has not allowed him to live."

verses.textZh: 但是保罗却把那条蛇抖在火里，自己一点也没有受伤。
verses.textZhCnvs: 但是保罗却把那条蛇抖在火里，自己一点也没有受伤。
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗竟把那毒蛇甩在火里，并没有受伤。
verses.textEnNiv: But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
verses.textEnEsv: He, however, shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.
verses.textEnNkjv: But he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.
verses.textEnNlt: But Paul shook off the snake into the fire and was unharmed.
verses.textEnNasb: However, Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no harm.
verses.textEn: But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.

verses.textZh: 他们等着看他发肿，或者忽然暴毙。但等了很久，见他平安无事，就转念说，他是个神明。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们等着看他发肿，或者忽然暴毙。但等了很久，见他平安无事，就转念说，他是个神明。
verses.textZhCuv: 土人想他必要肿起来，或是忽然仆倒死了；看了多时，见他无害，就转念，说：「他是个神。」
verses.textEnNiv: The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall dead; but after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
verses.textEnEsv: They were waiting for him to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But when they had waited a long time and saw no misfortune come to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.
verses.textEnNkjv: However, they were expecting that he would swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after they had looked for a long time and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.
verses.textEnNlt: The people waited for him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But when they had waited a long time and saw that he wasn’t harmed, they changed their minds and decided he was a god.
verses.textEnNasb: Now they were expecting that he was going to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after they had waited a long time and had seen nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and began to say that he was a god.
verses.textEn: The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall dead; but after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

verses.textZh: 那地附近有些田产，是岛上的首领部百流所拥有的。他欢迎我们，善意招待我们三天。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那地附近有些田产，是岛上的首领部百流所拥有的。他欢迎我们，善意招待我们三天。
verses.textZhCuv: 离那地方不远，有田产是岛长部百流的；他接纳我们，尽情款待三日。
verses.textEnNiv: There was an estate nearby that belonged to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us to his home and showed us generous hospitality for three days.
verses.textEnEsv: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
verses.textEnNkjv: In that region there was an estate of the leading citizen of the island, whose name was Publius, who received us and entertained us courteously for three days.
verses.textEnNlt: Near the shore where we landed was an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and treated us kindly for three days.
verses.textEnNasb: Now in the neighboring parts of that place were lands belonging to the leading man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and entertained us warmly for three days.
verses.textEn: There was an estate nearby that belonged to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us to his home and showed us generous hospitality for three days.

verses.textZh: 那时，部百流的父亲患了痢疾，发热卧病在床，保罗到他那里，为他祈祷按手，医好了他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那时，部百流的父亲患了痢疾，发热卧病在床，保罗到他那里，为他祈祷按手，医好了他。
verses.textZhCuv: 当时，部百流的父亲患热病和痢疾躺着。保罗进去，为他祷告，按手在他身上，治好了他。
verses.textEnNiv: His father was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him and, after prayer, placed his hands on him and healed him.
verses.textEnEsv: It happened that the father of Publius lay sick with fever and dysentery. And Paul visited him and prayed, and putting his hands on him, healed him.
verses.textEnNkjv: And it happened that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and dysentery. Paul went in to him and prayed, and he laid his hands on him and healed him.
verses.textEnNlt: As it happened, Publius’s father was ill with fever and dysentery. Paul went in and prayed for him, and laying his hands on him, he healed him.
verses.textEnNasb: And it happened that the father of Publius was lying in bed afflicted with a recurring fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after he prayed, he laid his hands on him and healed him.
verses.textEn: His father was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him and, after prayer, placed his hands on him and healed him.

verses.textZh: 这么一来，岛上其他有病的都来了，也都治好了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 这么一来，岛上其他有病的都来了，也都治好了。
verses.textZhCuv: 从此，岛上其余的病人也来，得了医治。
verses.textEnNiv: When this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured.
verses.textEnEsv: And when this had taken place, the rest of the people on the island who had diseases also came and were cured.
verses.textEnNkjv: So when this was done, the rest of those on the island who had diseases also came and were healed.
verses.textEnNlt: Then all the other sick people on the island came and were healed.
verses.textEnNasb: After this happened, the rest of the people on the island who had diseases were coming to him and being cured.
verses.textEn: When this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured.

verses.textZh: 他们多方面尊敬我们；到开船的时候，又把我们所需要的东西送来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们多方面尊敬我们；到开船的时候，又把我们所需要的东西送来。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们又多方地尊敬我们；到了开船的时候，也把我们所需用的送到船上。
verses.textEnNiv: They honored us in many ways; and when we were ready to sail, they furnished us with the supplies we needed.
verses.textEnEsv: They also honored us greatly, and when we were about to sail, they put on board whatever we needed.
verses.textEnNkjv: They also honored us in many ways; and when we departed, they provided such things as were necessary.
verses.textEnNlt: As a result we were showered with honors, and when the time came to sail, people supplied us with everything we would need for the trip.
verses.textEnNasb: They also showed us many honors, and when we were about to set sail, they supplied us with everything we needed.
verses.textEn: They honored us in many ways; and when we were ready to sail, they furnished us with the supplies we needed.

verses.textZh: 过了三个月，我们上了一艘亚历山太来的船。这船在岛上过冬，船的名字是"宙斯双子"。
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了三个月，我们上了一艘亚历山太来的船。这船在岛上过冬，船的名字是"宙斯双子"。
verses.textZhCuv: 过了三个月，我们上了亚历山大的船往前行；这船以「宙斯双子」为记，是在那海岛过了冬的。
verses.textEnNiv: After three months we put out to sea in a ship that had wintered in the island—it was an Alexandrian ship with the figurehead of the twin gods Castor and Pollux.
verses.textEnEsv: After three months we set sail in a ship that had wintered in the island, a ship of Alexandria, with the twin gods as a figurehead.
verses.textEnNkjv: After three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship whose figurehead was the Twin Brothers, which had wintered at the island.
verses.textEnNlt: It was three months after the shipwreck that we set sail on another ship that had wintered at the island—an Alexandrian ship with the twin gods as its figurehead.
verses.textEnNasb: After three months we set sail on an Alexandrian ship which had wintered at the island, and which had the Twin Brothers for its figurehead.
verses.textEn: After three months we put out to sea in a ship that had wintered in the island—it was an Alexandrian ship with the figurehead of the twin gods Castor and Pollux.

verses.textZh: 到了叙拉古，我们停留了三天。
verses.textZhCnvs: 到了叙拉古，我们停留了三天。
verses.textZhCuv: 到了叙拉古，我们停泊三日；
verses.textEnNiv: We put in at Syracuse and stayed there three days.
verses.textEnEsv: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there for three days.
verses.textEnNkjv: And landing at Syracuse, we stayed three days.
verses.textEnNlt: Our first stop was Syracuse, where we stayed three days.
verses.textEnNasb: After we put in at Syracuse, we stayed there for three days.
verses.textEn: We put in at Syracuse and stayed there three days.

verses.textZh: 从那里绕道航行，来到利基翁。过了一天，起了南风，第二天到达部丢利。
verses.textZhCnvs: 从那里绕道航行，来到利基翁。过了一天，起了南风，第二天到达部丢利。
verses.textZhCuv: 又从那里绕行，来到利基翁。过了一天，起了南风，第二天就来到部丢利。
verses.textEnNiv: From there we set sail and arrived at Rhegium. The next day the south wind came up, and on the following day we reached Puteoli.
verses.textEnEsv: And from there we made a circuit and arrived at Rhegium. And after one day a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
verses.textEnNkjv: From there we circled round and reached Rhegium. And after one day the south wind blew; and the next day we came to Puteoli,
verses.textEnNlt: From there we sailed across to Rhegium. A day later a south wind began blowing, so the following day we sailed up the coast to Puteoli.
verses.textEnNasb: From there we sailed around and arrived at Rhegium, and a day later a south wind came up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
verses.textEn: From there we set sail and arrived at Rhegium. The next day the south wind came up, and on the following day we reached Puteoli.

verses.textZh: 我们在那里遇见一些弟兄，他们邀请我们一同住了七天。这样，我们就来到了罗马。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们在那里遇见一些弟兄，他们邀请我们一同住了七天。这样，我们就来到了罗马。
verses.textZhCuv: 在那里遇见弟兄们，请我们与他们同住了七天。这样，我们来到罗马。
verses.textEnNiv: There we found some brothers and sisters who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.
verses.textEnEsv: There we found brothers and were invited to stay with them for seven days. And so we came to Rome.
verses.textEnNkjv: where we found brethren, and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we went toward Rome.
verses.textEnNlt: There we found some believers, who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.
verses.textEnNasb: There we found some brothers and sisters, and were invited to stay with them for seven days; and that is how we came to Rome.
verses.textEn: There we found some brothers and sisters who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.

verses.textZh: 弟兄们听到了我们的消息，就从罗马出来，在亚比乌和三馆迎接我们。保罗见了他们，就感谢神，胆子也壮了起来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 弟兄们听到了我们的消息，就从罗马出来，在亚比乌和三馆迎接我们。保罗见了他们，就感谢神，胆子也壮了起来。
verses.textZhCuv: 那里的弟兄们一听见我们的信息就出来，到亚比乌市和三馆地方迎接我们。保罗见了他们，就感谢神，放心壮胆。
verses.textEnNiv: The brothers and sisters there had heard that we were coming, and they traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. At the sight of these people Paul thanked God and was encouraged.
verses.textEnEsv: And the brothers there, when they heard about us, came as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns to meet us. On seeing them, Paul thanked God and took courage.
verses.textEnNkjv: And from there, when the brethren heard about us, they came to meet us as far as Appii Forum and Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
verses.textEnNlt: The brothers and sisters in Rome had heard we were coming, and they came to meet us at the Forum on the Appian Way. Others joined us at The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and thanked God.
verses.textEnNasb: And from there the brothers and sisters, when they heard about us, came as far as the Market of Appius and the Three Inns to meet us; and when Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
verses.textEn: The brothers and sisters there had heard that we were coming, and they traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. At the sight of these people Paul thanked God and was encouraged.

verses.textZh: 我们到了罗马，保罗获准独自与看守他的士兵居住。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们到了罗马，保罗获准独自与看守他的士兵居住。
verses.textZhCuv: 进了罗马城， 保罗蒙准和一个看守他的兵另住在一处。
verses.textEnNiv: When we got to Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
verses.textEnEsv: And when we came into Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself, with the soldier who guarded him.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard; but Paul was permitted to dwell by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
verses.textEnNlt: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to have his own private lodging, though he was guarded by a soldier.
verses.textEnNasb: When we entered Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself, with the soldier who was guarding him.
verses.textEn: When we got to Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him.

verses.textZh: 过了三天，保罗请犹太人的首领来。他们都到了，保罗说："各位弟兄，我虽然没有作过甚么事反对人民或者反对祖先的规例，却像囚犯被逮捕，从耶路撒冷交到罗马人的手里。
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了三天，保罗请犹太人的首领来。他们都到了，保罗说："各位弟兄，我虽然没有作过甚么事反对人民或者反对祖先的规例，却像囚犯被逮捕，从耶路撒冷交到罗马人的手里。
verses.textZhCuv: 过了三天，保罗请犹太人的首领来。他们来了，就对他们说：「弟兄们，我虽没有做什么事干犯本国的百姓和我们祖宗的规条，却被锁绑，从耶路撒冷解在罗马人的手里。
verses.textEnNiv: Three days later he called together the local Jewish leaders. When they had assembled, Paul said to them: "My brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or against the customs of our ancestors, I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
verses.textEnEsv: After three days he called together the local leaders of the Jews, and when they had gathered, he said to them, "Brothers, though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
verses.textEnNkjv: And it came to pass after three days that Paul called the leaders of the Jews together. So when they had come together, he said to them: "Men and brethren, though I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
verses.textEnNlt: Three days after Paul’s arrival, he called together the local Jewish leaders. He said to them, "Brothers, I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Roman government, even though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our ancestors.
verses.textEnNasb: After three days Paul called together those who were the leading men of the Jews, and when they came together, he began saying to them, "Brothers, though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, yet I was handed over to the Romans as a prisoner from Jerusalem.
verses.textEn: Three days later he called together the local Jewish leaders. When they had assembled, Paul said to them: "My brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or against the customs of our ancestors, I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.

verses.textZh: 他们审讯之后，因为在我身上没有甚么该死的罪，就想要释放我。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们审讯之后，因为在我身上没有甚么该死的罪，就想要释放我。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们审问了我，就愿意释放我；因为在我身上，并没有该死的罪。
verses.textEnNiv: They examined me and wanted to release me, because I was not guilty of any crime deserving death.
verses.textEnEsv: When they had examined me, they wished to set me at liberty, because there was no reason for the death penalty in my case.
verses.textEnNkjv: who, when they had examined me, wanted to let me go, because there was no cause for putting me to death.
verses.textEnNlt: The Romans tried me and wanted to release me, because they found no cause for the death sentence.
verses.textEnNasb: And when they had examined me, they were willing to release me because there were no grounds for putting me to death.
verses.textEn: They examined me and wanted to release me, because I was not guilty of any crime deserving death.

verses.textZh: 可是犹太人反对，我迫不得已才上诉凯撒，并不是有甚么事要控告我的国民。
verses.textZhCnvs: 可是犹太人反对，我迫不得已才上诉凯撒，并不是有甚么事要控告我的国民。
verses.textZhCuv: 无奈犹太人不服，我不得已，只好上告于凯撒，并非有什么事要控告我本国的百姓。
verses.textEnNiv: The Jews objected, so I was compelled to make an appeal to Caesar. I certainly did not intend to bring any charge against my own people.
verses.textEnEsv: But because the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar—though I had no charge to bring against my nation.
verses.textEnNkjv: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything of which to accuse my nation.
verses.textEnNlt: But when the Jewish leaders protested the decision, I felt it necessary to appeal to Caesar, even though I had no desire to press charges against my own people.
verses.textEnNasb: But when the Jews objected, I was forced to appeal to Caesar, not that I had any accusation against my nation.
verses.textEn: The Jews objected, so I was compelled to make an appeal to Caesar. I certainly did not intend to bring any charge against my own people.

verses.textZh: 因此，我请你们来见面谈谈。我原是为了以色列的盼望，才带上这条锁炼的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 因此，我请你们来见面谈谈。我原是为了以色列的盼望，才带上这条锁炼的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 因此，我请你们来见面说话，我原为以色列人所指望的，被这链子捆锁。」
verses.textEnNiv: For this reason I have asked to see you and talk with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain."
verses.textEnEsv: For this reason, therefore, I have asked to see you and speak with you, since it is because of the hope of Israel that I am wearing this chain."
verses.textEnNkjv: For this reason therefore I have called for you, to see you and speak with you, because for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain."
verses.textEnNlt: I asked you to come here today so we could get acquainted and so I could explain to you that I am bound with this chain because I believe that the hope of Israel—the Messiah—has already come."
verses.textEnNasb: For this reason, therefore, I requested to see you and to speak with you, since I am wearing this chain for the sake of the hope of Israel."
verses.textEn: For this reason I have asked to see you and talk with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain."

verses.textZh: 他们说："我们没有收到犹太来的信，是提到你的，弟兄中也没有人来报告，或说你甚么坏话。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们说："我们没有收到犹太来的信，是提到你的，弟兄中也没有人来报告，或说你甚么坏话。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们说：「我们并没有接着从犹太来论你的信，也没有弟兄到这里来报给我们说你有什么不好处。
verses.textEnNiv: They replied, "We have not received any letters from Judea concerning you, and none of our people who have come from there has reported or said anything bad about you.
verses.textEnEsv: And they said to him, "We have received no letters from Judea about you, and none of the brothers coming here has reported or spoken any evil about you.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then they said to him, "We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor have any of the brethren who came reported or spoken any evil of you.
verses.textEnNlt: They replied, "We have had no letters from Judea or reports against you from anyone who has come here.
verses.textEnNasb: They said to him, "We have neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor has any of the brothers come here and reported or spoken anything bad about you.
verses.textEn: They replied, "We have not received any letters from Judea concerning you, and none of our people who have come from there has reported or said anything bad about you.

verses.textZh: 但我们觉得应该听听你本人的意见，因为关于这教派，我们知道是到处遭人反对的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 但我们觉得应该听听你本人的意见，因为关于这教派，我们知道是到处遭人反对的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 但我们愿意听你的意见如何；因为这教门，我们晓得是到处被毁谤的。」
verses.textEnNiv: But we want to hear what your views are, for we know that people everywhere are talking against this sect."
verses.textEnEsv: But we desire to hear from you what your views are, for with regard to this sect we know that everywhere it is spoken against."
verses.textEnNkjv: But we desire to hear from you what you think; for concerning this sect, we know that it is spoken against everywhere."
verses.textEnNlt: But we want to hear what you believe, for the only thing we know about this movement is that it is denounced everywhere."
verses.textEnNasb: But we desire to hear from you what your views are; for regarding this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere."
verses.textEn: But we want to hear what your views are, for we know that people everywhere are talking against this sect."

verses.textZh: 他们和保罗约好了一个日子，到那日有很多人到他的住所来见他。他从早到晚向他们讲解，为神的国竭力作见证，引用摩西的律法和先知的话劝他们信耶稣。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们和保罗约好了一个日子，到那日有很多人到他的住所来见他。他从早到晚向他们讲解，为神的国竭力作见证，引用摩西的律法和先知的话劝他们信耶稣。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们和保罗约定了日子，就有许多人到他的寓处来。保罗从早到晚，对他们讲论这事，证明神国的道，引摩西的律法和先知的书，以耶稣的事劝勉他们。
verses.textEnNiv: They arranged to meet Paul on a certain day, and came in even larger numbers to the place where he was staying. He witnessed to them from morning till evening, explaining about the kingdom of God, and from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets he tried to persuade them about Jesus.
verses.textEnEsv: When they had appointed a day for him, they came to him at his lodging in greater numbers. From morning till evening he expounded to them, testifying to the kingdom of God and trying to convince them about Jesus both from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets.
verses.textEnNkjv: So when they had appointed him a day, many came to him at his lodging, to whom he explained and solemnly testified of the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets, from morning till evening.
verses.textEnNlt: So a time was set, and on that day a large number of people came to Paul’s lodging. He explained and testified about the Kingdom of God and tried to persuade them about Jesus from the Scriptures. Using the law of Moses and the books of the prophets, he spoke to them from morning until evening.
verses.textEnNasb: When they had set a day for Paul, people came to him at his lodging in large numbers; and he was explaining to them by solemnly testifying about the kingdom of God and trying to persuade them concerning Jesus, from both the Law of Moses and from the Prophets, from morning until evening.
verses.textEn: They arranged to meet Paul on a certain day, and came in even larger numbers to the place where he was staying. He witnessed to them from morning till evening, explaining about the kingdom of God, and from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets he tried to persuade them about Jesus.

verses.textZh: 他所说的话，有人信服，也有人不信。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他所说的话，有人信服，也有人不信。
verses.textZhCuv: 他所说的话，有信的，有不信的。
verses.textEnNiv: Some were convinced by what he said, but others would not believe.
verses.textEnEsv: And some were convinced by what he said, but others disbelieved.
verses.textEnNkjv: And some were persuaded by the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.
verses.textEnNlt: Some were persuaded by the things he said, but others did not believe.
verses.textEnNasb: Some were being persuaded by the things said by Paul, but others would not believe.
verses.textEn: Some were convinced by what he said, but others would not believe.

verses.textZh: 他们彼此不合，就分散了。未散以前，保罗说了几句话："圣灵藉以赛亚先知对你们祖先所说的，一点不错。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他们彼此不合，就分散了。未散以前，保罗说了几句话："圣灵藉以赛亚先知对你们祖先所说的，一点不错。
verses.textZhCuv: 他们彼此不合，就散了；未散以先，保罗说了一句话，说：「圣灵藉先知以赛亚向你们祖宗所说的话是不错的。
verses.textEnNiv: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: "The Holy Spirit spoke the truth to your ancestors when he said through Isaiah the prophet:
verses.textEnEsv: And disagreeing among themselves, they departed after Paul had made one statement: "The Holy Spirit was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
verses.textEnNkjv: So when they did not agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had said one word: "The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
verses.textEnNlt: And after they had argued back and forth among themselves, they left with this final word from Paul: "The Holy Spirit was right when he said to your ancestors through Isaiah the prophet,
verses.textEnNasb: And when they disagreed with one another, they began leaving after Paul said one parting statement: "The Holy Spirit rightly spoke through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,
verses.textEn: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: "The Holy Spirit spoke the truth to your ancestors when he said through Isaiah the prophet:

verses.textZh: 他说： ‘你去告诉这人民： 你们听是听见了，总是不明白； 看是看见了，总是不领悟。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他说： ‘你去告诉这人民： 你们听是听见了，总是不明白； 看是看见了，总是不领悟。
verses.textZhCuv: 他说： 你去告诉这百姓说： 你们听是要听见，却不明白； 看是要看见，却不晓得；
verses.textEnNiv: " ‘Go to this people and say, "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving."
verses.textEnEsv: "‘Go to this people, and say, "You will indeed hear but never understand, and you will indeed see but never perceive."
verses.textEnNkjv: saying, ‘Go to this people and say: "Hearing you will hear, and shall not understand; And seeing you will see, and not perceive;
verses.textEnNlt: ‘Go and say to this people: When you hear what I say, you will not understand. When you see what I do, you will not comprehend.
verses.textEnNasb: saying, ‘Go to this people and say, " You will keep on hearing, and will not understand; And you will keep on seeing, and will not perceive;
verses.textEn: " ‘Go to this people and say, "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving."

verses.textZh: 因为这人民的心思迟钝， 用不灵的耳朵去听， 又闭上了眼睛； 免得自己眼睛看见， 耳朵听见， 心里明白，回转过来， 我就医好他们。’
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为这人民的心思迟钝， 用不灵的耳朵去听， 又闭上了眼睛； 免得自己眼睛看见， 耳朵听见， 心里明白，回转过来， 我就医好他们。’
verses.textZhCuv: 因为这百姓油蒙了心， 耳朵发沉， 眼睛闭着； 恐怕眼睛看见， 耳朵听见， 心里明白，回转过来， 我就医治他们。
verses.textEnNiv: For this people’s heart has become calloused; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them.’
verses.textEnEsv: For this people’s heart has grown dull, and with their ears they can barely hear, and their eyes they have closed; lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them.’
verses.textEnNkjv: For the hearts of this people have grown dull. Their ears are hard of hearing, And their eyes they have closed, Lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, Lest they should understand with their hearts and turn, So that I should heal them." ’
verses.textEnNlt: For the hearts of these people are hardened, and their ears cannot hear, and they have closed their eyes— so their eyes cannot see, and their ears cannot hear, and their hearts cannot understand, and they cannot turn to me and let me heal them.’
verses.textEnNasb: For the hearts of this people have become insensitive, And with their ears they hardly hear, And they have closed their eyes; Otherwise they might see with their eyes, And hear with their ears, And understand with their heart and return, And I would heal them." ’
verses.textEn: For this people’s heart has become calloused; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them.’

verses.textZh: 所以你们应当知道，神这救恩，已经传给外族人，他们也必听从。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 所以你们应当知道，神这救恩，已经传给外族人，他们也必听从。"
verses.textZhCuv: 所以你们当知道，神这救恩，如今传给外邦人，他们也必听受。」
verses.textEnNiv: "Therefore I want you to know that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!"
verses.textEnEsv: Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen."
verses.textEnNkjv: "Therefore let it be known to you that the salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will hear it!"
verses.textEnNlt: So I want you to know that this salvation from God has also been offered to the Gentiles, and they will accept it."
verses.textEnNasb: Therefore, let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will also listen."
verses.textEn: "Therefore I want you to know that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!"

verses.textZh: 保罗在自己所租的房子里，住了整整两年。凡来见他的人，他都接待，
verses.textZhCnvs: 保罗在自己所租的房子里，住了整整两年。凡来见他的人，他都接待，
verses.textZhCuv: 保罗在自己所租的房子里住了足足两年。凡来见他的人，他全都接待，
verses.textEnNiv: For two whole years Paul stayed there in his own rented house and welcomed all who came to see him.
verses.textEnEsv: He lived there two whole years at his own expense, and welcomed all who came to him,
verses.textEnNkjv: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed and had a great dispute among themselves.
verses.textEnNlt: For the next two years, Paul lived in Rome at his own expense. He welcomed all who visited him,
verses.textEnNasb: Now Paul stayed two full years in his own rented lodging and welcomed all who came to him,
verses.textEn: For two whole years Paul stayed there in his own rented house and welcomed all who came to see him.

verses.textZh: 并且放胆地传讲神的国，教导有关主耶稣基督的事，没有受到甚么禁止。
verses.textZhCnvs: 并且放胆地传讲神的国，教导有关主耶稣基督的事，没有受到甚么禁止。
verses.textZhCuv: 放胆传讲神国的道，将主耶稣基督的事教导人，并没有人禁止。
verses.textEnNiv: He proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ—with all boldness and without hindrance!
verses.textEnEsv: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Paul dwelt two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who came to him,
verses.textEnNlt: boldly proclaiming the Kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ. And no one tried to stop him.
verses.textEnNasb: preaching the kingdom of God and teaching things about the Lord Jesus Christ with all openness, unhindered.
verses.textEn: He proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ—with all boldness and without hindrance!
